General Procedure 3: Screening of aryl halide, iron salt and ligand | In an argon-filled glovebox, an oven dried 7.5 mL vial was charged with the appropriate iron salt (0.02
M in THF, 0.5 mL, 0.01 mmol) and the appropriate ligand or ligand precursor (0.01 mmol), the resulting
mixture was allowed to stir at rt for 30 min. MgBr2·OEt2 (0.2 mL, 0.1 M in THF, 0.02 mmol), aryl halide
1 (0.1 mmol) and aryl boronate 2a (0.5 mL, 0.4 M in THF, 0.2 mmol) were then added to the vial
sequentially. The reaction mixture was then heated to 80 °C and stirred for 18 h. The resulting mixture
was cooled to room temperature and quenched with 1.0 M HCl (1.0 mL) before dodecane (internal
standard, 22.7 µL, 0.1 mmol) was added and the reaction mixture extracted into CH2Cl2 (5.0 mL). After
being thoroughly stirred, an aliquot was then taken and filtered through Celite (eluting with CH2Cl2)
and was then analysed by GC.

General Procedure 4: Screening of boronic esters | Under an N2 atmosphere, an oven dried Schlenk tube was charged with the appropriate boronic ester
(0.5 mmol) and then THF (3.0 mL) and the resultant solution cooled to -40 °C. tBuLi (0.29 mL, 1.7 M in
hexane, 0.5 mmol) was then added dropwise and the resultant mixture allowed to stir for 30 mins at
-40 °C. The reaction mixture was slowly brought to rt and stirred for a further 45 mins.
Meanwhile, in an argon-filled glovebox, IMes·HCl (8.6 mg, 0.025 mmol) and FeBr3 (7.4 mg, 0.025
mmol) were added to a dried Schleck tube, containing a stirrer bar, followed by THF (1.5 mL), and the
resultant mixture allowed to stir for 30 min at rt. MgBr2·OEt2 (12.9 mg, 0.05 mmol) and chlorobenzene
1a (25.5 µL, 0.25 mmol) were then added. The Schlenk tube was sealed and taken out of the glovebox
and attached to a Schlenk line and heated to an external temperature of 80 °C. The aryl boronate
formed in situ above was then added in one portion, the Schlenk was sealed, and the reaction mixture
was heated at 80 °C for 18 h. The resulting mixture was cooled to room temperature and quenched
with 1.0 M HCl (2.5 mL) and dodecane (internal standard, 56.8 µL, 0.25 mmol) was added. The organics
were extracted into CH2Cl2 (10 mL), and an aliquot was taken for analysis by GC.

In an argon-filled glovebox, IMes·HCl (8.6 mg, 0.025 mmol) and FeBr3 (7.4 mg, 0.025 mmol) were
added to an oven dried 7.5 mL vial, containing a stirrer bar, followed by 1,4-dioxane (1.5 mL), and the
resultant mixture was stirred for 30 min at rt. MgBr2·OEt2 (12.9 mg, 0.05 mmol) and chlorobenzene 1a
(25.5 µL, 0.25 mmol) were then added and the resultant mixture was stirred and heated to 100 °C.
MeMgBr (0.025 mL, 1.0 M in Et2O, 0.025 mmol) was then added to the vial and was allowed to stir for
5 mins, this was followed by a solution of aryl boronate 2a (0.33 M in 2-MeTHF). The vial was then
sealed, and the resultant reaction mixture was stirred and heated at 100 °C for 18 h. The resulting
mixture was cooled to room temperature and quenched with 1.0 M HCl (2.5 mL) and dodecane
(internal standard, 56.8 µL, 0.25 mmol) was added to the reaction mixture. The organics were
extracted into CH2Cl2 (10 mL), and an aliquot was taken for analysis by GC.

General Procedure 10: Electrophile screen | In an argon-filled glovebox, IMes·HCl (17.1 mg, 0.05 mmol), FeBr3 (14.8 mg, 0.05 mmol), MgBr2·OEt2
(25.8 mg, 0.1 mmol) and the appropriate aryl chloride 1 (0.5 mmol) were added to a dried Schleck
tube, containing a stirrer bar, followed by 1,4-dioxane (3.0 mL). In a separate dried Schlenk tube the
aryl boronate 2a (552.9 mg, 1.25 mmol) was dissolved in the 2-MeTHF (3.0 mL). Both Schlenk tubes
were sealed and taken out of the glove box and attached to a Schlenk line and heated to the
appropriate temperature (2-MeTHF 80 °C and 1,4-dioxane 100 °C) whilst being stirred. MeMgBr (0.05
mL, 1.0 M, 0.05 mmol) was added to the Schlenk tube containing the pre-catalyst mixture and the
resultant mixture was stirred for 5 mins. The aryl boronate-containing solution was then added quickly
to the Schlenk tube containing the pre-catalyst mixture and the resultant mixture was stirred and
heated at 100 °C (external temp.) for 3 hrs. The resulting mixture was cooled to room temperature
and quenched with 1.0 M HCl (5.0 mL). The organics were extracted with CH2Cl2 (3 x 10 mL), the
combined organic layers dried over MgSO4 and filtered. 1,3,5-Trimethoxybenzene (internal standard,
84.1 mg, 0.5 mmol) was added, and an aliquot taken for analysis by 1H NMR spectroscopy. The volatiles
were then removed under vacuum. The crude mixture was purified by flash column chromatography
(gradient elution: 100% hexanes to 25% ethyl acetate in hexanes) to yield the desired biaryl cross-
coupled product 3.

50 Analysis of the catalytic reaction using LIFDI-MS The LIFDI mass spectrometry was performed by the University of York mass spectrometry service. The LIFDI-MS spectra were measured using a JEOL AccuTOF GCx-plus (time of flight MS) fitted with a LIFDI probe (manufactured by Linden CMS GmbH, Germany) and utilizing a 13 μm activated tungsten emitter. Where possible, mass spectral data are quoted as the m/z ratio along with the relative peak height in brackets. Mass to charge ratios (m/z) are reported in Daltons.
The reaction protocol was modified in order to prepare appropriate samples for LIFDI-MS. The high
concentration of boronate ester 2a and the low-freezing point of 1,4-dioxane proved to be a challenge
when preparing samples for air-sensitive LIFDI-MS analysis.
Due to the low-freezing point of 1,4-dioxane, samples prepared in a 1:1 mixture of 2-MeTHF and 1,4-
dioxane froze on the LIFDI emitter in the MS source. Thus, the catalytic conditions were modified to
be carried in 2-MeTHF, at 80 °C for LIFDI-MS analysis. However, the use of chlorobenzene 1a in 2-
MeTHF also posed a challenge when collecting appropriate MS, and thus for certain reactions, THF at
Supplementary Figure 7 Samples dissolved in a mixture of 2-MeTHF:1,4-dioxane (1:1) froze on the
emitter of the LIFDI-MS instrument. This is likely due to the low-freezing point of 1,4-dioxane.
Additionally, samples with a high concentration of boronate ester 2a seemed to block the LIFDI
capillary and form a bubbling mass on the LIFDI emitter in the MS source. This was a prevalent issued
when samples taken from the Fe-catalytic reaction were run without any modification:

5.3 Determining the Orders in Pre-catalyst and Reagents | General Procedure 13: Kinetic experiments
The procedure below outlines the standard conditions that were employed in the kinetic experiments.
These were held constant when a given reaction component’s concentration was varied.
In an argon-filled glovebox, IMes·HCl (17.1 mg, 0.05 mmol), FeBr3 (14.8 mg, 0.05 mmol), MgBr2·OEt2
(25.8 mg, 0.1 mmol), dodecane (internal standard, 113.6 µL, 0.5 mmol), and chlorobenzene 1a (50.9
µL, 0.5 mmol) were added to an oven-dried Schleck tube containing a stirrer bar, followed by 1,4-
dioxane (3.0 mL), resulting in the formation of an orange suspension. In a separate dried Schlenk tube
the aryl boronate 2a (552.9 mg, 1.25 mmol) was dissolved in the 2-MeTHF (3.0 mL). Both Schlenk tubes
were sealed and taken out of the glove box and attached to a Schlenk line and heated to the
appropriate external temperature (2-MeTHF 80 °C and 1,4-dioxane 100 °C), whilst being stirred.
MeMgBr (0.05 mL, 1.0 M, 0.05 mmol) was added to the Schlenk tube containing the pre-catalyst
mixture and the resultant mixture was stirred for 5 mins. The aryl boronate-containing solution was
then added quickly to the Schlenk tube containing the pre-catalyst mixture, which was then sealed,
and the resultant reaction mixture was stirred and heated at 100 °C (external temp.). Aliquots (~0.05
mL) were taken at the times given. Each aliquot was quenched with 1.0 M HCl (0.1 mL) and extracted
into CH2Cl2 (2.0 mL) and then analysed by GC.

5.3 Determining the Orders in Pre-catalyst and Reagents | General Procedure 13: Kinetic experiments
The procedure below outlines the standard conditions that were employed in the kinetic experiments.
These were held constant when a given reaction component’s concentration was varied.
In an argon-filled glovebox, IMes·HCl (17.1 mg, 0.05 mmol), FeBr3 (14.8 mg, 0.05 mmol), MgBr2·OEt2
(25.8 mg, 0.1 mmol), dodecane (internal standard, 113.6 µL, 0.5 mmol), and chlorobenzene 1a (50.9
µL, 0.5 mmol) were added to an oven-dried Schleck tube containing a stirrer bar, followed by 1,4-
dioxane (3.0 mL), resulting in the formation of an orange suspension. In a separate dried Schlenk tube
the aryl boronate 2a (552.9 mg, 1.25 mmol) was dissolved in the 2-MeTHF (3.0 mL). Both Schlenk tubes
were sealed and taken out of the glove box and attached to a Schlenk line and heated to the
appropriate external temperature (2-MeTHF 80 °C and 1,4-dioxane 100 °C), whilst being stirred.
MeMgBr (0.05 mL, 1.0 M, 0.05 mmol) was added to the Schlenk tube containing the pre-catalyst
mixture and the resultant mixture was stirred for 5 mins. The aryl boronate-containing solution was
then added quickly to the Schlenk tube containing the pre-catalyst mixture, which was then sealed,
and the resultant reaction mixture was stirred and heated at 100 °C (external temp.). Aliquots (~0.05
mL) were taken at the times given. Each aliquot was quenched with 1.0 M HCl (0.1 mL) and extracted
into CH2Cl2 (2.0 mL) and then analysed by GC.

5.3 Determining the Orders in Pre-catalyst and Reagents | General Procedure 13: Kinetic experiments
The procedure below outlines the standard conditions that were employed in the kinetic experiments.
These were held constant when a given reaction component’s concentration was varied.
In an argon-filled glovebox, IMes·HCl (17.1 mg, 0.05 mmol), FeBr3 (14.8 mg, 0.05 mmol), MgBr2·OEt2
(25.8 mg, 0.1 mmol), dodecane (internal standard, 113.6 µL, 0.5 mmol), and chlorobenzene 1a (50.9
µL, 0.5 mmol) were added to an oven-dried Schleck tube containing a stirrer bar, followed by 1,4-
dioxane (3.0 mL), resulting in the formation of an orange suspension. In a separate dried Schlenk tube
the aryl boronate 2a (552.9 mg, 1.25 mmol) was dissolved in the 2-MeTHF (3.0 mL). Both Schlenk tubes
were sealed and taken out of the glove box and attached to a Schlenk line and heated to the
appropriate external temperature (2-MeTHF 80 °C and 1,4-dioxane 100 °C), whilst being stirred.
MeMgBr (0.05 mL, 1.0 M, 0.05 mmol) was added to the Schlenk tube containing the pre-catalyst
mixture and the resultant mixture was stirred for 5 mins. The aryl boronate-containing solution was
then added quickly to the Schlenk tube containing the pre-catalyst mixture, which was then sealed,
and the resultant reaction mixture was stirred and heated at 100 °C (external temp.). Aliquots (~0.05
mL) were taken at the times given. Each aliquot was quenched with 1.0 M HCl (0.1 mL) and extracted
into CH2Cl2 (2.0 mL) and then analysed by GC.

5.3 Determining the Orders in Pre-catalyst and Reagents | General Procedure 13: Kinetic experiments
The procedure below outlines the standard conditions that were employed in the kinetic experiments.
These were held constant when a given reaction component’s concentration was varied.
In an argon-filled glovebox, IMes·HCl (17.1 mg, 0.05 mmol), FeBr3 (14.8 mg, 0.05 mmol), MgBr2·OEt2
(25.8 mg, 0.1 mmol), dodecane (internal standard, 113.6 µL, 0.5 mmol), and chlorobenzene 1a (50.9
µL, 0.5 mmol) were added to an oven-dried Schleck tube containing a stirrer bar, followed by 1,4-
dioxane (3.0 mL), resulting in the formation of an orange suspension. In a separate dried Schlenk tube
the aryl boronate 2a (552.9 mg, 1.25 mmol) was dissolved in the 2-MeTHF (3.0 mL). Both Schlenk tubes
were sealed and taken out of the glove box and attached to a Schlenk line and heated to the
appropriate external temperature (2-MeTHF 80 °C and 1,4-dioxane 100 °C), whilst being stirred.
MeMgBr (0.05 mL, 1.0 M, 0.05 mmol) was added to the Schlenk tube containing the pre-catalyst
mixture and the resultant mixture was stirred for 5 mins. The aryl boronate-containing solution was
then added quickly to the Schlenk tube containing the pre-catalyst mixture, which was then sealed,
and the resultant reaction mixture was stirred and heated at 100 °C (external temp.). Aliquots (~0.05
mL) were taken at the times given. Each aliquot was quenched with 1.0 M HCl (0.1 mL) and extracted
into CH2Cl2 (2.0 mL) and then analysed by GC.

5.3 Determining the Orders in Pre-catalyst and Reagents | General Procedure 13: Kinetic experiments
The procedure below outlines the standard conditions that were employed in the kinetic experiments.
These were held constant when a given reaction component’s concentration was varied.
In an argon-filled glovebox, IMes·HCl (17.1 mg, 0.05 mmol), FeBr3 (14.8 mg, 0.05 mmol), MgBr2·OEt2
(25.8 mg, 0.1 mmol), dodecane (internal standard, 113.6 µL, 0.5 mmol), and chlorobenzene 1a (50.9
µL, 0.5 mmol) were added to an oven-dried Schleck tube containing a stirrer bar, followed by 1,4-
dioxane (3.0 mL), resulting in the formation of an orange suspension. In a separate dried Schlenk tube
the aryl boronate 2a (552.9 mg, 1.25 mmol) was dissolved in the 2-MeTHF (3.0 mL). Both Schlenk tubes
were sealed and taken out of the glove box and attached to a Schlenk line and heated to the
appropriate external temperature (2-MeTHF 80 °C and 1,4-dioxane 100 °C), whilst being stirred.
MeMgBr (0.05 mL, 1.0 M, 0.05 mmol) was added to the Schlenk tube containing the pre-catalyst
mixture and the resultant mixture was stirred for 5 mins. The aryl boronate-containing solution was
then added quickly to the Schlenk tube containing the pre-catalyst mixture, which was then sealed,
and the resultant reaction mixture was stirred and heated at 100 °C (external temp.). Aliquots (~0.05
mL) were taken at the times given. Each aliquot was quenched with 1.0 M HCl (0.1 mL) and extracted
into CH2Cl2 (2.0 mL) and then analysed by GC.

5.3 Determining the Orders in Pre-catalyst and Reagents | General Procedure 13: Kinetic experiments
The procedure below outlines the standard conditions that were employed in the kinetic experiments.
These were held constant when a given reaction component’s concentration was varied.
In an argon-filled glovebox, IMes·HCl (17.1 mg, 0.05 mmol), FeBr3 (14.8 mg, 0.05 mmol), MgBr2·OEt2
(25.8 mg, 0.1 mmol), dodecane (internal standard, 113.6 µL, 0.5 mmol), and chlorobenzene 1a (50.9
µL, 0.5 mmol) were added to an oven-dried Schleck tube containing a stirrer bar, followed by 1,4-
dioxane (3.0 mL), resulting in the formation of an orange suspension. In a separate dried Schlenk tube
the aryl boronate 2a (552.9 mg, 1.25 mmol) was dissolved in the 2-MeTHF (3.0 mL). Both Schlenk tubes
were sealed and taken out of the glove box and attached to a Schlenk line and heated to the
appropriate external temperature (2-MeTHF 80 °C and 1,4-dioxane 100 °C), whilst being stirred.
MeMgBr (0.05 mL, 1.0 M, 0.05 mmol) was added to the Schlenk tube containing the pre-catalyst
mixture and the resultant mixture was stirred for 5 mins. The aryl boronate-containing solution was
then added quickly to the Schlenk tube containing the pre-catalyst mixture, which was then sealed,
and the resultant reaction mixture was stirred and heated at 100 °C (external temp.). Aliquots (~0.05
mL) were taken at the times given. Each aliquot was quenched with 1.0 M HCl (0.1 mL) and extracted
into CH2Cl2 (2.0 mL) and then analysed by GC.

5.3 Determining the Orders in Pre-catalyst and Reagents | General Procedure 13: Kinetic experiments
The procedure below outlines the standard conditions that were employed in the kinetic experiments.
These were held constant when a given reaction component’s concentration was varied.
In an argon-filled glovebox, IMes·HCl (17.1 mg, 0.05 mmol), FeBr3 (14.8 mg, 0.05 mmol), MgBr2·OEt2
(25.8 mg, 0.1 mmol), dodecane (internal standard, 113.6 µL, 0.5 mmol), and chlorobenzene 1a (50.9
µL, 0.5 mmol) were added to an oven-dried Schleck tube containing a stirrer bar, followed by 1,4-
dioxane (3.0 mL), resulting in the formation of an orange suspension. In a separate dried Schlenk tube
the aryl boronate 2a (552.9 mg, 1.25 mmol) was dissolved in the 2-MeTHF (3.0 mL). Both Schlenk tubes
were sealed and taken out of the glove box and attached to a Schlenk line and heated to the
appropriate external temperature (2-MeTHF 80 °C and 1,4-dioxane 100 °C), whilst being stirred.
MeMgBr (0.05 mL, 1.0 M, 0.05 mmol) was added to the Schlenk tube containing the pre-catalyst
mixture and the resultant mixture was stirred for 5 mins. The aryl boronate-containing solution was
then added quickly to the Schlenk tube containing the pre-catalyst mixture, which was then sealed,
and the resultant reaction mixture was stirred and heated at 100 °C (external temp.). Aliquots (~0.05
mL) were taken at the times given. Each aliquot was quenched with 1.0 M HCl (0.1 mL) and extracted
into CH2Cl2 (2.0 mL) and then analysed by GC.

5.3 Determining the Orders in Pre-catalyst and Reagents | General Procedure 13: Kinetic experiments
The procedure below outlines the standard conditions that were employed in the kinetic experiments.
These were held constant when a given reaction component’s concentration was varied.
In an argon-filled glovebox, IMes·HCl (17.1 mg, 0.05 mmol), FeBr3 (14.8 mg, 0.05 mmol), MgBr2·OEt2
(25.8 mg, 0.1 mmol), dodecane (internal standard, 113.6 µL, 0.5 mmol), and chlorobenzene 1a (50.9
µL, 0.5 mmol) were added to an oven-dried Schleck tube containing a stirrer bar, followed by 1,4-
dioxane (3.0 mL), resulting in the formation of an orange suspension. In a separate dried Schlenk tube
the aryl boronate 2a (552.9 mg, 1.25 mmol) was dissolved in the 2-MeTHF (3.0 mL). Both Schlenk tubes
were sealed and taken out of the glove box and attached to a Schlenk line and heated to the
appropriate external temperature (2-MeTHF 80 °C and 1,4-dioxane 100 °C), whilst being stirred.
MeMgBr (0.05 mL, 1.0 M, 0.05 mmol) was added to the Schlenk tube containing the pre-catalyst
mixture and the resultant mixture was stirred for 5 mins. The aryl boronate-containing solution was
then added quickly to the Schlenk tube containing the pre-catalyst mixture, which was then sealed,
and the resultant reaction mixture was stirred and heated at 100 °C (external temp.). Aliquots (~0.05
mL) were taken at the times given. Each aliquot was quenched with 1.0 M HCl (0.1 mL) and extracted
into CH2Cl2 (2.0 mL) and then analysed by GC.

5.3 Determining the Orders in Pre-catalyst and Reagents | General Procedure 13: Kinetic experiments
The procedure below outlines the standard conditions that were employed in the kinetic experiments.
These were held constant when a given reaction component’s concentration was varied.
In an argon-filled glovebox, IMes·HCl (17.1 mg, 0.05 mmol), FeBr3 (14.8 mg, 0.05 mmol), MgBr2·OEt2
(25.8 mg, 0.1 mmol), dodecane (internal standard, 113.6 µL, 0.5 mmol), and chlorobenzene 1a (50.9
µL, 0.5 mmol) were added to an oven-dried Schleck tube containing a stirrer bar, followed by 1,4-
dioxane (3.0 mL), resulting in the formation of an orange suspension. In a separate dried Schlenk tube
the aryl boronate 2a (552.9 mg, 1.25 mmol) was dissolved in the 2-MeTHF (3.0 mL). Both Schlenk tubes
were sealed and taken out of the glove box and attached to a Schlenk line and heated to the
appropriate external temperature (2-MeTHF 80 °C and 1,4-dioxane 100 °C), whilst being stirred.
MeMgBr (0.05 mL, 1.0 M, 0.05 mmol) was added to the Schlenk tube containing the pre-catalyst
mixture and the resultant mixture was stirred for 5 mins. The aryl boronate-containing solution was
then added quickly to the Schlenk tube containing the pre-catalyst mixture, which was then sealed,
and the resultant reaction mixture was stirred and heated at 100 °C (external temp.). Aliquots (~0.05
mL) were taken at the times given. Each aliquot was quenched with 1.0 M HCl (0.1 mL) and extracted
into CH2Cl2 (2.0 mL) and then analysed by GC.

5.3 Determining the Orders in Pre-catalyst and Reagents | General Procedure 13: Kinetic experiments
The procedure below outlines the standard conditions that were employed in the kinetic experiments.
These were held constant when a given reaction component’s concentration was varied.
In an argon-filled glovebox, IMes·HCl (17.1 mg, 0.05 mmol), FeBr3 (14.8 mg, 0.05 mmol), MgBr2·OEt2
(25.8 mg, 0.1 mmol), dodecane (internal standard, 113.6 µL, 0.5 mmol), and chlorobenzene 1a (50.9
µL, 0.5 mmol) were added to an oven-dried Schleck tube containing a stirrer bar, followed by 1,4-
dioxane (3.0 mL), resulting in the formation of an orange suspension. In a separate dried Schlenk tube
the aryl boronate 2a (552.9 mg, 1.25 mmol) was dissolved in the 2-MeTHF (3.0 mL). Both Schlenk tubes
were sealed and taken out of the glove box and attached to a Schlenk line and heated to the
appropriate external temperature (2-MeTHF 80 °C and 1,4-dioxane 100 °C), whilst being stirred.
MeMgBr (0.05 mL, 1.0 M, 0.05 mmol) was added to the Schlenk tube containing the pre-catalyst
mixture and the resultant mixture was stirred for 5 mins. The aryl boronate-containing solution was
then added quickly to the Schlenk tube containing the pre-catalyst mixture, which was then sealed,
and the resultant reaction mixture was stirred and heated at 100 °C (external temp.). Aliquots (~0.05
mL) were taken at the times given. Each aliquot was quenched with 1.0 M HCl (0.1 mL) and extracted
into CH2Cl2 (2.0 mL) and then analysed by GC.

5.3 Determining the Orders in Pre-catalyst and Reagents | General Procedure 13: Kinetic experiments
The procedure below outlines the standard conditions that were employed in the kinetic experiments.
These were held constant when a given reaction component’s concentration was varied.
In an argon-filled glovebox, IMes·HCl (17.1 mg, 0.05 mmol), FeBr3 (14.8 mg, 0.05 mmol), MgBr2·OEt2
(25.8 mg, 0.1 mmol), dodecane (internal standard, 113.6 µL, 0.5 mmol), and chlorobenzene 1a (50.9
µL, 0.5 mmol) were added to an oven-dried Schleck tube containing a stirrer bar, followed by 1,4-
dioxane (3.0 mL), resulting in the formation of an orange suspension. In a separate dried Schlenk tube
the aryl boronate 2a (552.9 mg, 1.25 mmol) was dissolved in the 2-MeTHF (3.0 mL). Both Schlenk tubes
were sealed and taken out of the glove box and attached to a Schlenk line and heated to the
appropriate external temperature (2-MeTHF 80 °C and 1,4-dioxane 100 °C), whilst being stirred.
MeMgBr (0.05 mL, 1.0 M, 0.05 mmol) was added to the Schlenk tube containing the pre-catalyst
mixture and the resultant mixture was stirred for 5 mins. The aryl boronate-containing solution was
then added quickly to the Schlenk tube containing the pre-catalyst mixture, which was then sealed,
and the resultant reaction mixture was stirred and heated at 100 °C (external temp.). Aliquots (~0.05
mL) were taken at the times given. Each aliquot was quenched with 1.0 M HCl (0.1 mL) and extracted
into CH2Cl2 (2.0 mL) and then analysed by GC.

5.3 Determining the Orders in Pre-catalyst and Reagents | General Procedure 13: Kinetic experiments
The procedure below outlines the standard conditions that were employed in the kinetic experiments.
These were held constant when a given reaction component’s concentration was varied.
In an argon-filled glovebox, IMes·HCl (17.1 mg, 0.05 mmol), FeBr3 (14.8 mg, 0.05 mmol), MgBr2·OEt2
(25.8 mg, 0.1 mmol), dodecane (internal standard, 113.6 µL, 0.5 mmol), and chlorobenzene 1a (50.9
µL, 0.5 mmol) were added to an oven-dried Schleck tube containing a stirrer bar, followed by 1,4-
dioxane (3.0 mL), resulting in the formation of an orange suspension. In a separate dried Schlenk tube
the aryl boronate 2a (552.9 mg, 1.25 mmol) was dissolved in the 2-MeTHF (3.0 mL). Both Schlenk tubes
were sealed and taken out of the glove box and attached to a Schlenk line and heated to the
appropriate external temperature (2-MeTHF 80 °C and 1,4-dioxane 100 °C), whilst being stirred.
MeMgBr (0.05 mL, 1.0 M, 0.05 mmol) was added to the Schlenk tube containing the pre-catalyst
mixture and the resultant mixture was stirred for 5 mins. The aryl boronate-containing solution was
then added quickly to the Schlenk tube containing the pre-catalyst mixture, which was then sealed,
and the resultant reaction mixture was stirred and heated at 100 °C (external temp.). Aliquots (~0.05
mL) were taken at the times given. Each aliquot was quenched with 1.0 M HCl (0.1 mL) and extracted
into CH2Cl2 (2.0 mL) and then analysed by GC.

5.3 Determining the Orders in Pre-catalyst and Reagents | General Procedure 13: Kinetic experiments
The procedure below outlines the standard conditions that were employed in the kinetic experiments.
These were held constant when a given reaction component’s concentration was varied.
In an argon-filled glovebox, IMes·HCl (17.1 mg, 0.05 mmol), FeBr3 (14.8 mg, 0.05 mmol), MgBr2·OEt2
(25.8 mg, 0.1 mmol), dodecane (internal standard, 113.6 µL, 0.5 mmol), and chlorobenzene 1a (50.9
µL, 0.5 mmol) were added to an oven-dried Schleck tube containing a stirrer bar, followed by 1,4-
dioxane (3.0 mL), resulting in the formation of an orange suspension. In a separate dried Schlenk tube
the aryl boronate 2a (552.9 mg, 1.25 mmol) was dissolved in the 2-MeTHF (3.0 mL). Both Schlenk tubes
were sealed and taken out of the glove box and attached to a Schlenk line and heated to the
appropriate external temperature (2-MeTHF 80 °C and 1,4-dioxane 100 °C), whilst being stirred.
MeMgBr (0.05 mL, 1.0 M, 0.05 mmol) was added to the Schlenk tube containing the pre-catalyst
mixture and the resultant mixture was stirred for 5 mins. The aryl boronate-containing solution was
then added quickly to the Schlenk tube containing the pre-catalyst mixture, which was then sealed,
and the resultant reaction mixture was stirred and heated at 100 °C (external temp.). Aliquots (~0.05
mL) were taken at the times given. Each aliquot was quenched with 1.0 M HCl (0.1 mL) and extracted
into CH2Cl2 (2.0 mL) and then analysed by GC.

5.3 Determining the Orders in Pre-catalyst and Reagents | General Procedure 13: Kinetic experiments
The procedure below outlines the standard conditions that were employed in the kinetic experiments.
These were held constant when a given reaction component’s concentration was varied.
In an argon-filled glovebox, IMes·HCl (17.1 mg, 0.05 mmol), FeBr3 (14.8 mg, 0.05 mmol), MgBr2·OEt2
(25.8 mg, 0.1 mmol), dodecane (internal standard, 113.6 µL, 0.5 mmol), and chlorobenzene 1a (50.9
µL, 0.5 mmol) were added to an oven-dried Schleck tube containing a stirrer bar, followed by 1,4-
dioxane (3.0 mL), resulting in the formation of an orange suspension. In a separate dried Schlenk tube
the aryl boronate 2a (552.9 mg, 1.25 mmol) was dissolved in the 2-MeTHF (3.0 mL). Both Schlenk tubes
were sealed and taken out of the glove box and attached to a Schlenk line and heated to the
appropriate external temperature (2-MeTHF 80 °C and 1,4-dioxane 100 °C), whilst being stirred.
MeMgBr (0.05 mL, 1.0 M, 0.05 mmol) was added to the Schlenk tube containing the pre-catalyst
mixture and the resultant mixture was stirred for 5 mins. The aryl boronate-containing solution was
then added quickly to the Schlenk tube containing the pre-catalyst mixture, which was then sealed,
and the resultant reaction mixture was stirred and heated at 100 °C (external temp.). Aliquots (~0.05
mL) were taken at the times given. Each aliquot was quenched with 1.0 M HCl (0.1 mL) and extracted
into CH2Cl2 (2.0 mL) and then analysed by GC.

5.3 Determining the Orders in Pre-catalyst and Reagents | General Procedure 13: Kinetic experiments
The procedure below outlines the standard conditions that were employed in the kinetic experiments.
These were held constant when a given reaction component’s concentration was varied.
In an argon-filled glovebox, IMes·HCl (17.1 mg, 0.05 mmol), FeBr3 (14.8 mg, 0.05 mmol), MgBr2·OEt2
(25.8 mg, 0.1 mmol), dodecane (internal standard, 113.6 µL, 0.5 mmol), and chlorobenzene 1a (50.9
µL, 0.5 mmol) were added to an oven-dried Schleck tube containing a stirrer bar, followed by 1,4-
dioxane (3.0 mL), resulting in the formation of an orange suspension. In a separate dried Schlenk tube
the aryl boronate 2a (552.9 mg, 1.25 mmol) was dissolved in the 2-MeTHF (3.0 mL). Both Schlenk tubes
were sealed and taken out of the glove box and attached to a Schlenk line and heated to the
appropriate external temperature (2-MeTHF 80 °C and 1,4-dioxane 100 °C), whilst being stirred.
MeMgBr (0.05 mL, 1.0 M, 0.05 mmol) was added to the Schlenk tube containing the pre-catalyst
mixture and the resultant mixture was stirred for 5 mins. The aryl boronate-containing solution was
then added quickly to the Schlenk tube containing the pre-catalyst mixture, which was then sealed,
and the resultant reaction mixture was stirred and heated at 100 °C (external temp.). Aliquots (~0.05
mL) were taken at the times given. Each aliquot was quenched with 1.0 M HCl (0.1 mL) and extracted
into CH2Cl2 (2.0 mL) and then analysed by GC.

5.3 Determining the Orders in Pre-catalyst and Reagents | General Procedure 13: Kinetic experiments
The procedure below outlines the standard conditions that were employed in the kinetic experiments.
These were held constant when a given reaction component’s concentration was varied.
In an argon-filled glovebox, IMes·HCl (17.1 mg, 0.05 mmol), FeBr3 (14.8 mg, 0.05 mmol), MgBr2·OEt2
(25.8 mg, 0.1 mmol), dodecane (internal standard, 113.6 µL, 0.5 mmol), and chlorobenzene 1a (50.9
µL, 0.5 mmol) were added to an oven-dried Schleck tube containing a stirrer bar, followed by 1,4-
dioxane (3.0 mL), resulting in the formation of an orange suspension. In a separate dried Schlenk tube
the aryl boronate 2a (552.9 mg, 1.25 mmol) was dissolved in the 2-MeTHF (3.0 mL). Both Schlenk tubes
were sealed and taken out of the glove box and attached to a Schlenk line and heated to the
appropriate external temperature (2-MeTHF 80 °C and 1,4-dioxane 100 °C), whilst being stirred.
MeMgBr (0.05 mL, 1.0 M, 0.05 mmol) was added to the Schlenk tube containing the pre-catalyst
mixture and the resultant mixture was stirred for 5 mins. The aryl boronate-containing solution was
then added quickly to the Schlenk tube containing the pre-catalyst mixture, which was then sealed,
and the resultant reaction mixture was stirred and heated at 100 °C (external temp.). Aliquots (~0.05
mL) were taken at the times given. Each aliquot was quenched with 1.0 M HCl (0.1 mL) and extracted
into CH2Cl2 (2.0 mL) and then analysed by GC.

5.3 Determining the Orders in Pre-catalyst and Reagents | General Procedure 13: Kinetic experiments
The procedure below outlines the standard conditions that were employed in the kinetic experiments.
These were held constant when a given reaction component’s concentration was varied.
In an argon-filled glovebox, IMes·HCl (17.1 mg, 0.05 mmol), FeBr3 (14.8 mg, 0.05 mmol), MgBr2·OEt2
(25.8 mg, 0.1 mmol), dodecane (internal standard, 113.6 µL, 0.5 mmol), and chlorobenzene 1a (50.9
µL, 0.5 mmol) were added to an oven-dried Schleck tube containing a stirrer bar, followed by 1,4-
dioxane (3.0 mL), resulting in the formation of an orange suspension. In a separate dried Schlenk tube
the aryl boronate 2a (552.9 mg, 1.25 mmol) was dissolved in the 2-MeTHF (3.0 mL). Both Schlenk tubes
were sealed and taken out of the glove box and attached to a Schlenk line and heated to the
appropriate external temperature (2-MeTHF 80 °C and 1,4-dioxane 100 °C), whilst being stirred.
MeMgBr (0.05 mL, 1.0 M, 0.05 mmol) was added to the Schlenk tube containing the pre-catalyst
mixture and the resultant mixture was stirred for 5 mins. The aryl boronate-containing solution was
then added quickly to the Schlenk tube containing the pre-catalyst mixture, which was then sealed,
and the resultant reaction mixture was stirred and heated at 100 °C (external temp.). Aliquots (~0.05
mL) were taken at the times given. Each aliquot was quenched with 1.0 M HCl (0.1 mL) and extracted
into CH2Cl2 (2.0 mL) and then analysed by GC.

5.3 Determining the Orders in Pre-catalyst and Reagents | General Procedure 13: Kinetic experiments
The procedure below outlines the standard conditions that were employed in the kinetic experiments.
These were held constant when a given reaction component’s concentration was varied.
In an argon-filled glovebox, IMes·HCl (17.1 mg, 0.05 mmol), FeBr3 (14.8 mg, 0.05 mmol), MgBr2·OEt2
(25.8 mg, 0.1 mmol), dodecane (internal standard, 113.6 µL, 0.5 mmol), and chlorobenzene 1a (50.9
µL, 0.5 mmol) were added to an oven-dried Schleck tube containing a stirrer bar, followed by 1,4-
dioxane (3.0 mL), resulting in the formation of an orange suspension. In a separate dried Schlenk tube
the aryl boronate 2a (552.9 mg, 1.25 mmol) was dissolved in the 2-MeTHF (3.0 mL). Both Schlenk tubes
were sealed and taken out of the glove box and attached to a Schlenk line and heated to the
appropriate external temperature (2-MeTHF 80 °C and 1,4-dioxane 100 °C), whilst being stirred.
MeMgBr (0.05 mL, 1.0 M, 0.05 mmol) was added to the Schlenk tube containing the pre-catalyst
mixture and the resultant mixture was stirred for 5 mins. The aryl boronate-containing solution was
then added quickly to the Schlenk tube containing the pre-catalyst mixture, which was then sealed,
and the resultant reaction mixture was stirred and heated at 100 °C (external temp.). Aliquots (~0.05
mL) were taken at the times given. Each aliquot was quenched with 1.0 M HCl (0.1 mL) and extracted
into CH2Cl2 (2.0 mL) and then analysed by GC.

5.3 Determining the Orders in Pre-catalyst and Reagents | General Procedure 13: Kinetic experiments
The procedure below outlines the standard conditions that were employed in the kinetic experiments.
These were held constant when a given reaction component’s concentration was varied.
In an argon-filled glovebox, IMes·HCl (17.1 mg, 0.05 mmol), FeBr3 (14.8 mg, 0.05 mmol), MgBr2·OEt2
(25.8 mg, 0.1 mmol), dodecane (internal standard, 113.6 µL, 0.5 mmol), and chlorobenzene 1a (50.9
µL, 0.5 mmol) were added to an oven-dried Schleck tube containing a stirrer bar, followed by 1,4-
dioxane (3.0 mL), resulting in the formation of an orange suspension. In a separate dried Schlenk tube
the aryl boronate 2a (552.9 mg, 1.25 mmol) was dissolved in the 2-MeTHF (3.0 mL). Both Schlenk tubes
were sealed and taken out of the glove box and attached to a Schlenk line and heated to the
appropriate external temperature (2-MeTHF 80 °C and 1,4-dioxane 100 °C), whilst being stirred.
MeMgBr (0.05 mL, 1.0 M, 0.05 mmol) was added to the Schlenk tube containing the pre-catalyst
mixture and the resultant mixture was stirred for 5 mins. The aryl boronate-containing solution was
then added quickly to the Schlenk tube containing the pre-catalyst mixture, which was then sealed,
and the resultant reaction mixture was stirred and heated at 100 °C (external temp.). Aliquots (~0.05
mL) were taken at the times given. Each aliquot was quenched with 1.0 M HCl (0.1 mL) and extracted
into CH2Cl2 (2.0 mL) and then analysed by GC.

5.3 Determining the Orders in Pre-catalyst and Reagents | General Procedure 13: Kinetic experiments
The procedure below outlines the standard conditions that were employed in the kinetic experiments.
These were held constant when a given reaction component’s concentration was varied.
In an argon-filled glovebox, IMes·HCl (17.1 mg, 0.05 mmol), FeBr3 (14.8 mg, 0.05 mmol), MgBr2·OEt2
(25.8 mg, 0.1 mmol), dodecane (internal standard, 113.6 µL, 0.5 mmol), and chlorobenzene 1a (50.9
µL, 0.5 mmol) were added to an oven-dried Schleck tube containing a stirrer bar, followed by 1,4-
dioxane (3.0 mL), resulting in the formation of an orange suspension. In a separate dried Schlenk tube
the aryl boronate 2a (552.9 mg, 1.25 mmol) was dissolved in the 2-MeTHF (3.0 mL). Both Schlenk tubes
were sealed and taken out of the glove box and attached to a Schlenk line and heated to the
appropriate external temperature (2-MeTHF 80 °C and 1,4-dioxane 100 °C), whilst being stirred.
MeMgBr (0.05 mL, 1.0 M, 0.05 mmol) was added to the Schlenk tube containing the pre-catalyst
mixture and the resultant mixture was stirred for 5 mins. The aryl boronate-containing solution was
then added quickly to the Schlenk tube containing the pre-catalyst mixture, which was then sealed,
and the resultant reaction mixture was stirred and heated at 100 °C (external temp.). Aliquots (~0.05
mL) were taken at the times given. Each aliquot was quenched with 1.0 M HCl (0.1 mL) and extracted
into CH2Cl2 (2.0 mL) and then analysed by GC.

5.3 Determining the Orders in Pre-catalyst and Reagents | General Procedure 13: Kinetic experiments
The procedure below outlines the standard conditions that were employed in the kinetic experiments.
These were held constant when a given reaction component’s concentration was varied.
In an argon-filled glovebox, IMes·HCl (17.1 mg, 0.05 mmol), FeBr3 (14.8 mg, 0.05 mmol), MgBr2·OEt2
(25.8 mg, 0.1 mmol), dodecane (internal standard, 113.6 µL, 0.5 mmol), and chlorobenzene 1a (50.9
µL, 0.5 mmol) were added to an oven-dried Schleck tube containing a stirrer bar, followed by 1,4-
dioxane (3.0 mL), resulting in the formation of an orange suspension. In a separate dried Schlenk tube
the aryl boronate 2a (552.9 mg, 1.25 mmol) was dissolved in the 2-MeTHF (3.0 mL). Both Schlenk tubes
were sealed and taken out of the glove box and attached to a Schlenk line and heated to the
appropriate external temperature (2-MeTHF 80 °C and 1,4-dioxane 100 °C), whilst being stirred.
MeMgBr (0.05 mL, 1.0 M, 0.05 mmol) was added to the Schlenk tube containing the pre-catalyst
mixture and the resultant mixture was stirred for 5 mins. The aryl boronate-containing solution was
then added quickly to the Schlenk tube containing the pre-catalyst mixture, which was then sealed,
and the resultant reaction mixture was stirred and heated at 100 °C (external temp.). Aliquots (~0.05
mL) were taken at the times given. Each aliquot was quenched with 1.0 M HCl (0.1 mL) and extracted
into CH2Cl2 (2.0 mL) and then analysed by GC.

5.3 Determining the Orders in Pre-catalyst and Reagents | General Procedure 13: Kinetic experiments
The procedure below outlines the standard conditions that were employed in the kinetic experiments.
These were held constant when a given reaction component’s concentration was varied.
In an argon-filled glovebox, IMes·HCl (17.1 mg, 0.05 mmol), FeBr3 (14.8 mg, 0.05 mmol), MgBr2·OEt2
(25.8 mg, 0.1 mmol), dodecane (internal standard, 113.6 µL, 0.5 mmol), and chlorobenzene 1a (50.9
µL, 0.5 mmol) were added to an oven-dried Schleck tube containing a stirrer bar, followed by 1,4-
dioxane (3.0 mL), resulting in the formation of an orange suspension. In a separate dried Schlenk tube
the aryl boronate 2a (552.9 mg, 1.25 mmol) was dissolved in the 2-MeTHF (3.0 mL). Both Schlenk tubes
were sealed and taken out of the glove box and attached to a Schlenk line and heated to the
appropriate external temperature (2-MeTHF 80 °C and 1,4-dioxane 100 °C), whilst being stirred.
MeMgBr (0.05 mL, 1.0 M, 0.05 mmol) was added to the Schlenk tube containing the pre-catalyst
mixture and the resultant mixture was stirred for 5 mins. The aryl boronate-containing solution was
then added quickly to the Schlenk tube containing the pre-catalyst mixture, which was then sealed,
and the resultant reaction mixture was stirred and heated at 100 °C (external temp.). Aliquots (~0.05
mL) were taken at the times given. Each aliquot was quenched with 1.0 M HCl (0.1 mL) and extracted
into CH2Cl2 (2.0 mL) and then analysed by GC.

5.3 Determining the Orders in Pre-catalyst and Reagents | General Procedure 13: Kinetic experiments
The procedure below outlines the standard conditions that were employed in the kinetic experiments.
These were held constant when a given reaction component’s concentration was varied.
In an argon-filled glovebox, IMes·HCl (17.1 mg, 0.05 mmol), FeBr3 (14.8 mg, 0.05 mmol), MgBr2·OEt2
(25.8 mg, 0.1 mmol), dodecane (internal standard, 113.6 µL, 0.5 mmol), and chlorobenzene 1a (50.9
µL, 0.5 mmol) were added to an oven-dried Schleck tube containing a stirrer bar, followed by 1,4-
dioxane (3.0 mL), resulting in the formation of an orange suspension. In a separate dried Schlenk tube
the aryl boronate 2a (552.9 mg, 1.25 mmol) was dissolved in the 2-MeTHF (3.0 mL). Both Schlenk tubes
were sealed and taken out of the glove box and attached to a Schlenk line and heated to the
appropriate external temperature (2-MeTHF 80 °C and 1,4-dioxane 100 °C), whilst being stirred.
MeMgBr (0.05 mL, 1.0 M, 0.05 mmol) was added to the Schlenk tube containing the pre-catalyst
mixture and the resultant mixture was stirred for 5 mins. The aryl boronate-containing solution was
then added quickly to the Schlenk tube containing the pre-catalyst mixture, which was then sealed,
and the resultant reaction mixture was stirred and heated at 100 °C (external temp.). Aliquots (~0.05
mL) were taken at the times given. Each aliquot was quenched with 1.0 M HCl (0.1 mL) and extracted
into CH2Cl2 (2.0 mL) and then analysed by GC.

5.3 Determining the Orders in Pre-catalyst and Reagents | General Procedure 13: Kinetic experiments
The procedure below outlines the standard conditions that were employed in the kinetic experiments.
These were held constant when a given reaction component’s concentration was varied.
In an argon-filled glovebox, IMes·HCl (17.1 mg, 0.05 mmol), FeBr3 (14.8 mg, 0.05 mmol), MgBr2·OEt2
(25.8 mg, 0.1 mmol), dodecane (internal standard, 113.6 µL, 0.5 mmol), and chlorobenzene 1a (50.9
µL, 0.5 mmol) were added to an oven-dried Schleck tube containing a stirrer bar, followed by 1,4-
dioxane (3.0 mL), resulting in the formation of an orange suspension. In a separate dried Schlenk tube
the aryl boronate 2a (552.9 mg, 1.25 mmol) was dissolved in the 2-MeTHF (3.0 mL). Both Schlenk tubes
were sealed and taken out of the glove box and attached to a Schlenk line and heated to the
appropriate external temperature (2-MeTHF 80 °C and 1,4-dioxane 100 °C), whilst being stirred.
MeMgBr (0.05 mL, 1.0 M, 0.05 mmol) was added to the Schlenk tube containing the pre-catalyst
mixture and the resultant mixture was stirred for 5 mins. The aryl boronate-containing solution was
then added quickly to the Schlenk tube containing the pre-catalyst mixture, which was then sealed,
and the resultant reaction mixture was stirred and heated at 100 °C (external temp.). Aliquots (~0.05
mL) were taken at the times given. Each aliquot was quenched with 1.0 M HCl (0.1 mL) and extracted
into CH2Cl2 (2.0 mL) and then analysed by GC.

5.3 Determining the Orders in Pre-catalyst and Reagents | General Procedure 13: Kinetic experiments
The procedure below outlines the standard conditions that were employed in the kinetic experiments.
These were held constant when a given reaction component’s concentration was varied.
In an argon-filled glovebox, IMes·HCl (17.1 mg, 0.05 mmol), FeBr3 (14.8 mg, 0.05 mmol), MgBr2·OEt2
(25.8 mg, 0.1 mmol), dodecane (internal standard, 113.6 µL, 0.5 mmol), and chlorobenzene 1a (50.9
µL, 0.5 mmol) were added to an oven-dried Schleck tube containing a stirrer bar, followed by 1,4-
dioxane (3.0 mL), resulting in the formation of an orange suspension. In a separate dried Schlenk tube
the aryl boronate 2a (552.9 mg, 1.25 mmol) was dissolved in the 2-MeTHF (3.0 mL). Both Schlenk tubes
were sealed and taken out of the glove box and attached to a Schlenk line and heated to the
appropriate external temperature (2-MeTHF 80 °C and 1,4-dioxane 100 °C), whilst being stirred.
MeMgBr (0.05 mL, 1.0 M, 0.05 mmol) was added to the Schlenk tube containing the pre-catalyst
mixture and the resultant mixture was stirred for 5 mins. The aryl boronate-containing solution was
then added quickly to the Schlenk tube containing the pre-catalyst mixture, which was then sealed,
and the resultant reaction mixture was stirred and heated at 100 °C (external temp.). Aliquots (~0.05
mL) were taken at the times given. Each aliquot was quenched with 1.0 M HCl (0.1 mL) and extracted
into CH2Cl2 (2.0 mL) and then analysed by GC.

5.3 Determining the Orders in Pre-catalyst and Reagents | General Procedure 13: Kinetic experiments
The procedure below outlines the standard conditions that were employed in the kinetic experiments.
These were held constant when a given reaction component’s concentration was varied.
In an argon-filled glovebox, IMes·HCl (17.1 mg, 0.05 mmol), FeBr3 (14.8 mg, 0.05 mmol), MgBr2·OEt2
(25.8 mg, 0.1 mmol), dodecane (internal standard, 113.6 µL, 0.5 mmol), and chlorobenzene 1a (50.9
µL, 0.5 mmol) were added to an oven-dried Schleck tube containing a stirrer bar, followed by 1,4-
dioxane (3.0 mL), resulting in the formation of an orange suspension. In a separate dried Schlenk tube
the aryl boronate 2a (552.9 mg, 1.25 mmol) was dissolved in the 2-MeTHF (3.0 mL). Both Schlenk tubes
were sealed and taken out of the glove box and attached to a Schlenk line and heated to the
appropriate external temperature (2-MeTHF 80 °C and 1,4-dioxane 100 °C), whilst being stirred.
MeMgBr (0.05 mL, 1.0 M, 0.05 mmol) was added to the Schlenk tube containing the pre-catalyst
mixture and the resultant mixture was stirred for 5 mins. The aryl boronate-containing solution was
then added quickly to the Schlenk tube containing the pre-catalyst mixture, which was then sealed,
and the resultant reaction mixture was stirred and heated at 100 °C (external temp.). Aliquots (~0.05
mL) were taken at the times given. Each aliquot was quenched with 1.0 M HCl (0.1 mL) and extracted
into CH2Cl2 (2.0 mL) and then analysed by GC.

5.3 Determining the Orders in Pre-catalyst and Reagents | General Procedure 13: Kinetic experiments
The procedure below outlines the standard conditions that were employed in the kinetic experiments.
These were held constant when a given reaction component’s concentration was varied.
In an argon-filled glovebox, IMes·HCl (17.1 mg, 0.05 mmol), FeBr3 (14.8 mg, 0.05 mmol), MgBr2·OEt2
(25.8 mg, 0.1 mmol), dodecane (internal standard, 113.6 µL, 0.5 mmol), and chlorobenzene 1a (50.9
µL, 0.5 mmol) were added to an oven-dried Schleck tube containing a stirrer bar, followed by 1,4-
dioxane (3.0 mL), resulting in the formation of an orange suspension. In a separate dried Schlenk tube
the aryl boronate 2a (552.9 mg, 1.25 mmol) was dissolved in the 2-MeTHF (3.0 mL). Both Schlenk tubes
were sealed and taken out of the glove box and attached to a Schlenk line and heated to the
appropriate external temperature (2-MeTHF 80 °C and 1,4-dioxane 100 °C), whilst being stirred.
MeMgBr (0.05 mL, 1.0 M, 0.05 mmol) was added to the Schlenk tube containing the pre-catalyst
mixture and the resultant mixture was stirred for 5 mins. The aryl boronate-containing solution was
then added quickly to the Schlenk tube containing the pre-catalyst mixture, which was then sealed,
and the resultant reaction mixture was stirred and heated at 100 °C (external temp.). Aliquots (~0.05
mL) were taken at the times given. Each aliquot was quenched with 1.0 M HCl (0.1 mL) and extracted
into CH2Cl2 (2.0 mL) and then analysed by GC.

5.3 Determining the Orders in Pre-catalyst and Reagents | General Procedure 13: Kinetic experiments
The procedure below outlines the standard conditions that were employed in the kinetic experiments.
These were held constant when a given reaction component’s concentration was varied.
In an argon-filled glovebox, IMes·HCl (17.1 mg, 0.05 mmol), FeBr3 (14.8 mg, 0.05 mmol), MgBr2·OEt2
(25.8 mg, 0.1 mmol), dodecane (internal standard, 113.6 µL, 0.5 mmol), and chlorobenzene 1a (50.9
µL, 0.5 mmol) were added to an oven-dried Schleck tube containing a stirrer bar, followed by 1,4-
dioxane (3.0 mL), resulting in the formation of an orange suspension. In a separate dried Schlenk tube
the aryl boronate 2a (552.9 mg, 1.25 mmol) was dissolved in the 2-MeTHF (3.0 mL). Both Schlenk tubes
were sealed and taken out of the glove box and attached to a Schlenk line and heated to the
appropriate external temperature (2-MeTHF 80 °C and 1,4-dioxane 100 °C), whilst being stirred.
MeMgBr (0.05 mL, 1.0 M, 0.05 mmol) was added to the Schlenk tube containing the pre-catalyst
mixture and the resultant mixture was stirred for 5 mins. The aryl boronate-containing solution was
then added quickly to the Schlenk tube containing the pre-catalyst mixture, which was then sealed,
and the resultant reaction mixture was stirred and heated at 100 °C (external temp.). Aliquots (~0.05
mL) were taken at the times given. Each aliquot was quenched with 1.0 M HCl (0.1 mL) and extracted
into CH2Cl2 (2.0 mL) and then analysed by GC.

5.3 Determining the Orders in Pre-catalyst and Reagents | General Procedure 13: Kinetic experiments
The procedure below outlines the standard conditions that were employed in the kinetic experiments.
These were held constant when a given reaction component’s concentration was varied.
In an argon-filled glovebox, IMes·HCl (17.1 mg, 0.05 mmol), FeBr3 (14.8 mg, 0.05 mmol), MgBr2·OEt2
(25.8 mg, 0.1 mmol), dodecane (internal standard, 113.6 µL, 0.5 mmol), and chlorobenzene 1a (50.9
µL, 0.5 mmol) were added to an oven-dried Schleck tube containing a stirrer bar, followed by 1,4-
dioxane (3.0 mL), resulting in the formation of an orange suspension. In a separate dried Schlenk tube
the aryl boronate 2a (552.9 mg, 1.25 mmol) was dissolved in the 2-MeTHF (3.0 mL). Both Schlenk tubes
were sealed and taken out of the glove box and attached to a Schlenk line and heated to the
appropriate external temperature (2-MeTHF 80 °C and 1,4-dioxane 100 °C), whilst being stirred.
MeMgBr (0.05 mL, 1.0 M, 0.05 mmol) was added to the Schlenk tube containing the pre-catalyst
mixture and the resultant mixture was stirred for 5 mins. The aryl boronate-containing solution was
then added quickly to the Schlenk tube containing the pre-catalyst mixture, which was then sealed,
and the resultant reaction mixture was stirred and heated at 100 °C (external temp.). Aliquots (~0.05
mL) were taken at the times given. Each aliquot was quenched with 1.0 M HCl (0.1 mL) and extracted
into CH2Cl2 (2.0 mL) and then analysed by GC.

5.3 Determining the Orders in Pre-catalyst and Reagents | General Procedure 13: Kinetic experiments
The procedure below outlines the standard conditions that were employed in the kinetic experiments.
These were held constant when a given reaction component’s concentration was varied.
In an argon-filled glovebox, IMes·HCl (17.1 mg, 0.05 mmol), FeBr3 (14.8 mg, 0.05 mmol), MgBr2·OEt2
(25.8 mg, 0.1 mmol), dodecane (internal standard, 113.6 µL, 0.5 mmol), and chlorobenzene 1a (50.9
µL, 0.5 mmol) were added to an oven-dried Schleck tube containing a stirrer bar, followed by 1,4-
dioxane (3.0 mL), resulting in the formation of an orange suspension. In a separate dried Schlenk tube
the aryl boronate 2a (552.9 mg, 1.25 mmol) was dissolved in the 2-MeTHF (3.0 mL). Both Schlenk tubes
were sealed and taken out of the glove box and attached to a Schlenk line and heated to the
appropriate external temperature (2-MeTHF 80 °C and 1,4-dioxane 100 °C), whilst being stirred.
MeMgBr (0.05 mL, 1.0 M, 0.05 mmol) was added to the Schlenk tube containing the pre-catalyst
mixture and the resultant mixture was stirred for 5 mins. The aryl boronate-containing solution was
then added quickly to the Schlenk tube containing the pre-catalyst mixture, which was then sealed,
and the resultant reaction mixture was stirred and heated at 100 °C (external temp.). Aliquots (~0.05
mL) were taken at the times given. Each aliquot was quenched with 1.0 M HCl (0.1 mL) and extracted
into CH2Cl2 (2.0 mL) and then analysed by GC.

5.3 Determining the Orders in Pre-catalyst and Reagents | General Procedure 13: Kinetic experiments
The procedure below outlines the standard conditions that were employed in the kinetic experiments.
These were held constant when a given reaction component’s concentration was varied.
In an argon-filled glovebox, IMes·HCl (17.1 mg, 0.05 mmol), FeBr3 (14.8 mg, 0.05 mmol), MgBr2·OEt2
(25.8 mg, 0.1 mmol), dodecane (internal standard, 113.6 µL, 0.5 mmol), and chlorobenzene 1a (50.9
µL, 0.5 mmol) were added to an oven-dried Schleck tube containing a stirrer bar, followed by 1,4-
dioxane (3.0 mL), resulting in the formation of an orange suspension. In a separate dried Schlenk tube
the aryl boronate 2a (552.9 mg, 1.25 mmol) was dissolved in the 2-MeTHF (3.0 mL). Both Schlenk tubes
were sealed and taken out of the glove box and attached to a Schlenk line and heated to the
appropriate external temperature (2-MeTHF 80 °C and 1,4-dioxane 100 °C), whilst being stirred.
MeMgBr (0.05 mL, 1.0 M, 0.05 mmol) was added to the Schlenk tube containing the pre-catalyst
mixture and the resultant mixture was stirred for 5 mins. The aryl boronate-containing solution was
then added quickly to the Schlenk tube containing the pre-catalyst mixture, which was then sealed,
and the resultant reaction mixture was stirred and heated at 100 °C (external temp.). Aliquots (~0.05
mL) were taken at the times given. Each aliquot was quenched with 1.0 M HCl (0.1 mL) and extracted
into CH2Cl2 (2.0 mL) and then analysed by GC.

5.3 Determining the Orders in Pre-catalyst and Reagents | General Procedure 13: Kinetic experiments
The procedure below outlines the standard conditions that were employed in the kinetic experiments.
These were held constant when a given reaction component’s concentration was varied.
In an argon-filled glovebox, IMes·HCl (17.1 mg, 0.05 mmol), FeBr3 (14.8 mg, 0.05 mmol), MgBr2·OEt2
(25.8 mg, 0.1 mmol), dodecane (internal standard, 113.6 µL, 0.5 mmol), and chlorobenzene 1a (50.9
µL, 0.5 mmol) were added to an oven-dried Schleck tube containing a stirrer bar, followed by 1,4-
dioxane (3.0 mL), resulting in the formation of an orange suspension. In a separate dried Schlenk tube
the aryl boronate 2a (552.9 mg, 1.25 mmol) was dissolved in the 2-MeTHF (3.0 mL). Both Schlenk tubes
were sealed and taken out of the glove box and attached to a Schlenk line and heated to the
appropriate external temperature (2-MeTHF 80 °C and 1,4-dioxane 100 °C), whilst being stirred.
MeMgBr (0.05 mL, 1.0 M, 0.05 mmol) was added to the Schlenk tube containing the pre-catalyst
mixture and the resultant mixture was stirred for 5 mins. The aryl boronate-containing solution was
then added quickly to the Schlenk tube containing the pre-catalyst mixture, which was then sealed,
and the resultant reaction mixture was stirred and heated at 100 °C (external temp.). Aliquots (~0.05
mL) were taken at the times given. Each aliquot was quenched with 1.0 M HCl (0.1 mL) and extracted
into CH2Cl2 (2.0 mL) and then analysed by GC.

5.3 Determining the Orders in Pre-catalyst and Reagents | General Procedure 13: Kinetic experiments
The procedure below outlines the standard conditions that were employed in the kinetic experiments.
These were held constant when a given reaction component’s concentration was varied.
In an argon-filled glovebox, IMes·HCl (17.1 mg, 0.05 mmol), FeBr3 (14.8 mg, 0.05 mmol), MgBr2·OEt2
(25.8 mg, 0.1 mmol), dodecane (internal standard, 113.6 µL, 0.5 mmol), and chlorobenzene 1a (50.9
µL, 0.5 mmol) were added to an oven-dried Schleck tube containing a stirrer bar, followed by 1,4-
dioxane (3.0 mL), resulting in the formation of an orange suspension. In a separate dried Schlenk tube
the aryl boronate 2a (552.9 mg, 1.25 mmol) was dissolved in the 2-MeTHF (3.0 mL). Both Schlenk tubes
were sealed and taken out of the glove box and attached to a Schlenk line and heated to the
appropriate external temperature (2-MeTHF 80 °C and 1,4-dioxane 100 °C), whilst being stirred.
MeMgBr (0.05 mL, 1.0 M, 0.05 mmol) was added to the Schlenk tube containing the pre-catalyst
mixture and the resultant mixture was stirred for 5 mins. The aryl boronate-containing solution was
then added quickly to the Schlenk tube containing the pre-catalyst mixture, which was then sealed,
and the resultant reaction mixture was stirred and heated at 100 °C (external temp.). Aliquots (~0.05
mL) were taken at the times given. Each aliquot was quenched with 1.0 M HCl (0.1 mL) and extracted
into CH2Cl2 (2.0 mL) and then analysed by GC.

5.3 Determining the Orders in Pre-catalyst and Reagents | General Procedure 13: Kinetic experiments
The procedure below outlines the standard conditions that were employed in the kinetic experiments.
These were held constant when a given reaction component’s concentration was varied.
In an argon-filled glovebox, IMes·HCl (17.1 mg, 0.05 mmol), FeBr3 (14.8 mg, 0.05 mmol), MgBr2·OEt2
(25.8 mg, 0.1 mmol), dodecane (internal standard, 113.6 µL, 0.5 mmol), and chlorobenzene 1a (50.9
µL, 0.5 mmol) were added to an oven-dried Schleck tube containing a stirrer bar, followed by 1,4-
dioxane (3.0 mL), resulting in the formation of an orange suspension. In a separate dried Schlenk tube
the aryl boronate 2a (552.9 mg, 1.25 mmol) was dissolved in the 2-MeTHF (3.0 mL). Both Schlenk tubes
were sealed and taken out of the glove box and attached to a Schlenk line and heated to the
appropriate external temperature (2-MeTHF 80 °C and 1,4-dioxane 100 °C), whilst being stirred.
MeMgBr (0.05 mL, 1.0 M, 0.05 mmol) was added to the Schlenk tube containing the pre-catalyst
mixture and the resultant mixture was stirred for 5 mins. The aryl boronate-containing solution was
then added quickly to the Schlenk tube containing the pre-catalyst mixture, which was then sealed,
and the resultant reaction mixture was stirred and heated at 100 °C (external temp.). Aliquots (~0.05
mL) were taken at the times given. Each aliquot was quenched with 1.0 M HCl (0.1 mL) and extracted
into CH2Cl2 (2.0 mL) and then analysed by GC.

5.3 Determining the Orders in Pre-catalyst and Reagents | General Procedure 13: Kinetic experiments
The procedure below outlines the standard conditions that were employed in the kinetic experiments.
These were held constant when a given reaction component’s concentration was varied.
In an argon-filled glovebox, IMes·HCl (17.1 mg, 0.05 mmol), FeBr3 (14.8 mg, 0.05 mmol), MgBr2·OEt2
(25.8 mg, 0.1 mmol), dodecane (internal standard, 113.6 µL, 0.5 mmol), and chlorobenzene 1a (50.9
µL, 0.5 mmol) were added to an oven-dried Schleck tube containing a stirrer bar, followed by 1,4-
dioxane (3.0 mL), resulting in the formation of an orange suspension. In a separate dried Schlenk tube
the aryl boronate 2a (552.9 mg, 1.25 mmol) was dissolved in the 2-MeTHF (3.0 mL). Both Schlenk tubes
were sealed and taken out of the glove box and attached to a Schlenk line and heated to the
appropriate external temperature (2-MeTHF 80 °C and 1,4-dioxane 100 °C), whilst being stirred.
MeMgBr (0.05 mL, 1.0 M, 0.05 mmol) was added to the Schlenk tube containing the pre-catalyst
mixture and the resultant mixture was stirred for 5 mins. The aryl boronate-containing solution was
then added quickly to the Schlenk tube containing the pre-catalyst mixture, which was then sealed,
and the resultant reaction mixture was stirred and heated at 100 °C (external temp.). Aliquots (~0.05
mL) were taken at the times given. Each aliquot was quenched with 1.0 M HCl (0.1 mL) and extracted
into CH2Cl2 (2.0 mL) and then analysed by GC.

5.3 Determining the Orders in Pre-catalyst and Reagents | General Procedure 13: Kinetic experiments
The procedure below outlines the standard conditions that were employed in the kinetic experiments.
These were held constant when a given reaction component’s concentration was varied.
In an argon-filled glovebox, IMes·HCl (17.1 mg, 0.05 mmol), FeBr3 (14.8 mg, 0.05 mmol), MgBr2·OEt2
(25.8 mg, 0.1 mmol), dodecane (internal standard, 113.6 µL, 0.5 mmol), and chlorobenzene 1a (50.9
µL, 0.5 mmol) were added to an oven-dried Schleck tube containing a stirrer bar, followed by 1,4-
dioxane (3.0 mL), resulting in the formation of an orange suspension. In a separate dried Schlenk tube
the aryl boronate 2a (552.9 mg, 1.25 mmol) was dissolved in the 2-MeTHF (3.0 mL). Both Schlenk tubes
were sealed and taken out of the glove box and attached to a Schlenk line and heated to the
appropriate external temperature (2-MeTHF 80 °C and 1,4-dioxane 100 °C), whilst being stirred.
MeMgBr (0.05 mL, 1.0 M, 0.05 mmol) was added to the Schlenk tube containing the pre-catalyst
mixture and the resultant mixture was stirred for 5 mins. The aryl boronate-containing solution was
then added quickly to the Schlenk tube containing the pre-catalyst mixture, which was then sealed,
and the resultant reaction mixture was stirred and heated at 100 °C (external temp.). Aliquots (~0.05
mL) were taken at the times given. Each aliquot was quenched with 1.0 M HCl (0.1 mL) and extracted
into CH2Cl2 (2.0 mL) and then analysed by GC.

5.3 Determining the Orders in Pre-catalyst and Reagents | General Procedure 13: Kinetic experiments
The procedure below outlines the standard conditions that were employed in the kinetic experiments.
These were held constant when a given reaction component’s concentration was varied.
In an argon-filled glovebox, IMes·HCl (17.1 mg, 0.05 mmol), FeBr3 (14.8 mg, 0.05 mmol), MgBr2·OEt2
(25.8 mg, 0.1 mmol), dodecane (internal standard, 113.6 µL, 0.5 mmol), and chlorobenzene 1a (50.9
µL, 0.5 mmol) were added to an oven-dried Schleck tube containing a stirrer bar, followed by 1,4-
dioxane (3.0 mL), resulting in the formation of an orange suspension. In a separate dried Schlenk tube
the aryl boronate 2a (552.9 mg, 1.25 mmol) was dissolved in the 2-MeTHF (3.0 mL). Both Schlenk tubes
were sealed and taken out of the glove box and attached to a Schlenk line and heated to the
appropriate external temperature (2-MeTHF 80 °C and 1,4-dioxane 100 °C), whilst being stirred.
MeMgBr (0.05 mL, 1.0 M, 0.05 mmol) was added to the Schlenk tube containing the pre-catalyst
mixture and the resultant mixture was stirred for 5 mins. The aryl boronate-containing solution was
then added quickly to the Schlenk tube containing the pre-catalyst mixture, which was then sealed,
and the resultant reaction mixture was stirred and heated at 100 °C (external temp.). Aliquots (~0.05
mL) were taken at the times given. Each aliquot was quenched with 1.0 M HCl (0.1 mL) and extracted
into CH2Cl2 (2.0 mL) and then analysed by GC.

5.3 Determining the Orders in Pre-catalyst and Reagents | General Procedure 13: Kinetic experiments
The procedure below outlines the standard conditions that were employed in the kinetic experiments.
These were held constant when a given reaction component’s concentration was varied.
In an argon-filled glovebox, IMes·HCl (17.1 mg, 0.05 mmol), FeBr3 (14.8 mg, 0.05 mmol), MgBr2·OEt2
(25.8 mg, 0.1 mmol), dodecane (internal standard, 113.6 µL, 0.5 mmol), and chlorobenzene 1a (50.9
µL, 0.5 mmol) were added to an oven-dried Schleck tube containing a stirrer bar, followed by 1,4-
dioxane (3.0 mL), resulting in the formation of an orange suspension. In a separate dried Schlenk tube
the aryl boronate 2a (552.9 mg, 1.25 mmol) was dissolved in the 2-MeTHF (3.0 mL). Both Schlenk tubes
were sealed and taken out of the glove box and attached to a Schlenk line and heated to the
appropriate external temperature (2-MeTHF 80 °C and 1,4-dioxane 100 °C), whilst being stirred.
MeMgBr (0.05 mL, 1.0 M, 0.05 mmol) was added to the Schlenk tube containing the pre-catalyst
mixture and the resultant mixture was stirred for 5 mins. The aryl boronate-containing solution was
then added quickly to the Schlenk tube containing the pre-catalyst mixture, which was then sealed,
and the resultant reaction mixture was stirred and heated at 100 °C (external temp.). Aliquots (~0.05
mL) were taken at the times given. Each aliquot was quenched with 1.0 M HCl (0.1 mL) and extracted
into CH2Cl2 (2.0 mL) and then analysed by GC.

5.3 Determining the Orders in Pre-catalyst and Reagents | General Procedure 13: Kinetic experiments
The procedure below outlines the standard conditions that were employed in the kinetic experiments.
These were held constant when a given reaction component’s concentration was varied.
In an argon-filled glovebox, IMes·HCl (17.1 mg, 0.05 mmol), FeBr3 (14.8 mg, 0.05 mmol), MgBr2·OEt2
(25.8 mg, 0.1 mmol), dodecane (internal standard, 113.6 µL, 0.5 mmol), and chlorobenzene 1a (50.9
µL, 0.5 mmol) were added to an oven-dried Schleck tube containing a stirrer bar, followed by 1,4-
dioxane (3.0 mL), resulting in the formation of an orange suspension. In a separate dried Schlenk tube
the aryl boronate 2a (552.9 mg, 1.25 mmol) was dissolved in the 2-MeTHF (3.0 mL). Both Schlenk tubes
were sealed and taken out of the glove box and attached to a Schlenk line and heated to the
appropriate external temperature (2-MeTHF 80 °C and 1,4-dioxane 100 °C), whilst being stirred.
MeMgBr (0.05 mL, 1.0 M, 0.05 mmol) was added to the Schlenk tube containing the pre-catalyst
mixture and the resultant mixture was stirred for 5 mins. The aryl boronate-containing solution was
then added quickly to the Schlenk tube containing the pre-catalyst mixture, which was then sealed,
and the resultant reaction mixture was stirred and heated at 100 °C (external temp.). Aliquots (~0.05
mL) were taken at the times given. Each aliquot was quenched with 1.0 M HCl (0.1 mL) and extracted
into CH2Cl2 (2.0 mL) and then analysed by GC.

5.3 Determining the Orders in Pre-catalyst and Reagents | General Procedure 13: Kinetic experiments
The procedure below outlines the standard conditions that were employed in the kinetic experiments.
These were held constant when a given reaction component’s concentration was varied.
In an argon-filled glovebox, IMes·HCl (17.1 mg, 0.05 mmol), FeBr3 (14.8 mg, 0.05 mmol), MgBr2·OEt2
(25.8 mg, 0.1 mmol), dodecane (internal standard, 113.6 µL, 0.5 mmol), and chlorobenzene 1a (50.9
µL, 0.5 mmol) were added to an oven-dried Schleck tube containing a stirrer bar, followed by 1,4-
dioxane (3.0 mL), resulting in the formation of an orange suspension. In a separate dried Schlenk tube
the aryl boronate 2a (552.9 mg, 1.25 mmol) was dissolved in the 2-MeTHF (3.0 mL). Both Schlenk tubes
were sealed and taken out of the glove box and attached to a Schlenk line and heated to the
appropriate external temperature (2-MeTHF 80 °C and 1,4-dioxane 100 °C), whilst being stirred.
MeMgBr (0.05 mL, 1.0 M, 0.05 mmol) was added to the Schlenk tube containing the pre-catalyst
mixture and the resultant mixture was stirred for 5 mins. The aryl boronate-containing solution was
then added quickly to the Schlenk tube containing the pre-catalyst mixture, which was then sealed,
and the resultant reaction mixture was stirred and heated at 100 °C (external temp.). Aliquots (~0.05
mL) were taken at the times given. Each aliquot was quenched with 1.0 M HCl (0.1 mL) and extracted
into CH2Cl2 (2.0 mL) and then analysed by GC.

5.3 Determining the Orders in Pre-catalyst and Reagents | General Procedure 13: Kinetic experiments
The procedure below outlines the standard conditions that were employed in the kinetic experiments.
These were held constant when a given reaction component’s concentration was varied.
In an argon-filled glovebox, IMes·HCl (17.1 mg, 0.05 mmol), FeBr3 (14.8 mg, 0.05 mmol), MgBr2·OEt2
(25.8 mg, 0.1 mmol), dodecane (internal standard, 113.6 µL, 0.5 mmol), and chlorobenzene 1a (50.9
µL, 0.5 mmol) were added to an oven-dried Schleck tube containing a stirrer bar, followed by 1,4-
dioxane (3.0 mL), resulting in the formation of an orange suspension. In a separate dried Schlenk tube
the aryl boronate 2a (552.9 mg, 1.25 mmol) was dissolved in the 2-MeTHF (3.0 mL). Both Schlenk tubes
were sealed and taken out of the glove box and attached to a Schlenk line and heated to the
appropriate external temperature (2-MeTHF 80 °C and 1,4-dioxane 100 °C), whilst being stirred.
MeMgBr (0.05 mL, 1.0 M, 0.05 mmol) was added to the Schlenk tube containing the pre-catalyst
mixture and the resultant mixture was stirred for 5 mins. The aryl boronate-containing solution was
then added quickly to the Schlenk tube containing the pre-catalyst mixture, which was then sealed,
and the resultant reaction mixture was stirred and heated at 100 °C (external temp.). Aliquots (~0.05
mL) were taken at the times given. Each aliquot was quenched with 1.0 M HCl (0.1 mL) and extracted
into CH2Cl2 (2.0 mL) and then analysed by GC.

5.3 Determining the Orders in Pre-catalyst and Reagents | General Procedure 13: Kinetic experiments
The procedure below outlines the standard conditions that were employed in the kinetic experiments.
These were held constant when a given reaction component’s concentration was varied.
In an argon-filled glovebox, IMes·HCl (17.1 mg, 0.05 mmol), FeBr3 (14.8 mg, 0.05 mmol), MgBr2·OEt2
(25.8 mg, 0.1 mmol), dodecane (internal standard, 113.6 µL, 0.5 mmol), and chlorobenzene 1a (50.9
µL, 0.5 mmol) were added to an oven-dried Schleck tube containing a stirrer bar, followed by 1,4-
dioxane (3.0 mL), resulting in the formation of an orange suspension. In a separate dried Schlenk tube
the aryl boronate 2a (552.9 mg, 1.25 mmol) was dissolved in the 2-MeTHF (3.0 mL). Both Schlenk tubes
were sealed and taken out of the glove box and attached to a Schlenk line and heated to the
appropriate external temperature (2-MeTHF 80 °C and 1,4-dioxane 100 °C), whilst being stirred.
MeMgBr (0.05 mL, 1.0 M, 0.05 mmol) was added to the Schlenk tube containing the pre-catalyst
mixture and the resultant mixture was stirred for 5 mins. The aryl boronate-containing solution was
then added quickly to the Schlenk tube containing the pre-catalyst mixture, which was then sealed,
and the resultant reaction mixture was stirred and heated at 100 °C (external temp.). Aliquots (~0.05
mL) were taken at the times given. Each aliquot was quenched with 1.0 M HCl (0.1 mL) and extracted
into CH2Cl2 (2.0 mL) and then analysed by GC.

5.3 Determining the Orders in Pre-catalyst and Reagents | General Procedure 13: Kinetic experiments
The procedure below outlines the standard conditions that were employed in the kinetic experiments.
These were held constant when a given reaction component’s concentration was varied.
In an argon-filled glovebox, IMes·HCl (17.1 mg, 0.05 mmol), FeBr3 (14.8 mg, 0.05 mmol), MgBr2·OEt2
(25.8 mg, 0.1 mmol), dodecane (internal standard, 113.6 µL, 0.5 mmol), and chlorobenzene 1a (50.9
µL, 0.5 mmol) were added to an oven-dried Schleck tube containing a stirrer bar, followed by 1,4-
dioxane (3.0 mL), resulting in the formation of an orange suspension. In a separate dried Schlenk tube
the aryl boronate 2a (552.9 mg, 1.25 mmol) was dissolved in the 2-MeTHF (3.0 mL). Both Schlenk tubes
were sealed and taken out of the glove box and attached to a Schlenk line and heated to the
appropriate external temperature (2-MeTHF 80 °C and 1,4-dioxane 100 °C), whilst being stirred.
MeMgBr (0.05 mL, 1.0 M, 0.05 mmol) was added to the Schlenk tube containing the pre-catalyst
mixture and the resultant mixture was stirred for 5 mins. The aryl boronate-containing solution was
then added quickly to the Schlenk tube containing the pre-catalyst mixture, which was then sealed,
and the resultant reaction mixture was stirred and heated at 100 °C (external temp.). Aliquots (~0.05
mL) were taken at the times given. Each aliquot was quenched with 1.0 M HCl (0.1 mL) and extracted
into CH2Cl2 (2.0 mL) and then analysed by GC.

5.3 Determining the Orders in Pre-catalyst and Reagents | General Procedure 13: Kinetic experiments
The procedure below outlines the standard conditions that were employed in the kinetic experiments.
These were held constant when a given reaction component’s concentration was varied.
In an argon-filled glovebox, IMes·HCl (17.1 mg, 0.05 mmol), FeBr3 (14.8 mg, 0.05 mmol), MgBr2·OEt2
(25.8 mg, 0.1 mmol), dodecane (internal standard, 113.6 µL, 0.5 mmol), and chlorobenzene 1a (50.9
µL, 0.5 mmol) were added to an oven-dried Schleck tube containing a stirrer bar, followed by 1,4-
dioxane (3.0 mL), resulting in the formation of an orange suspension. In a separate dried Schlenk tube
the aryl boronate 2a (552.9 mg, 1.25 mmol) was dissolved in the 2-MeTHF (3.0 mL). Both Schlenk tubes
were sealed and taken out of the glove box and attached to a Schlenk line and heated to the
appropriate external temperature (2-MeTHF 80 °C and 1,4-dioxane 100 °C), whilst being stirred.
MeMgBr (0.05 mL, 1.0 M, 0.05 mmol) was added to the Schlenk tube containing the pre-catalyst
mixture and the resultant mixture was stirred for 5 mins. The aryl boronate-containing solution was
then added quickly to the Schlenk tube containing the pre-catalyst mixture, which was then sealed,
and the resultant reaction mixture was stirred and heated at 100 °C (external temp.). Aliquots (~0.05
mL) were taken at the times given. Each aliquot was quenched with 1.0 M HCl (0.1 mL) and extracted
into CH2Cl2 (2.0 mL) and then analysed by GC.

5.3 Determining the Orders in Pre-catalyst and Reagents | General Procedure 13: Kinetic experiments
The procedure below outlines the standard conditions that were employed in the kinetic experiments.
These were held constant when a given reaction component’s concentration was varied.
In an argon-filled glovebox, IMes·HCl (17.1 mg, 0.05 mmol), FeBr3 (14.8 mg, 0.05 mmol), MgBr2·OEt2
(25.8 mg, 0.1 mmol), dodecane (internal standard, 113.6 µL, 0.5 mmol), and chlorobenzene 1a (50.9
µL, 0.5 mmol) were added to an oven-dried Schleck tube containing a stirrer bar, followed by 1,4-
dioxane (3.0 mL), resulting in the formation of an orange suspension. In a separate dried Schlenk tube
the aryl boronate 2a (552.9 mg, 1.25 mmol) was dissolved in the 2-MeTHF (3.0 mL). Both Schlenk tubes
were sealed and taken out of the glove box and attached to a Schlenk line and heated to the
appropriate external temperature (2-MeTHF 80 °C and 1,4-dioxane 100 °C), whilst being stirred.
MeMgBr (0.05 mL, 1.0 M, 0.05 mmol) was added to the Schlenk tube containing the pre-catalyst
mixture and the resultant mixture was stirred for 5 mins. The aryl boronate-containing solution was
then added quickly to the Schlenk tube containing the pre-catalyst mixture, which was then sealed,
and the resultant reaction mixture was stirred and heated at 100 °C (external temp.). Aliquots (~0.05
mL) were taken at the times given. Each aliquot was quenched with 1.0 M HCl (0.1 mL) and extracted
into CH2Cl2 (2.0 mL) and then analysed by GC.

5.3 Determining the Orders in Pre-catalyst and Reagents | General Procedure 13: Kinetic experiments
The procedure below outlines the standard conditions that were employed in the kinetic experiments.
These were held constant when a given reaction component’s concentration was varied.
In an argon-filled glovebox, IMes·HCl (17.1 mg, 0.05 mmol), FeBr3 (14.8 mg, 0.05 mmol), MgBr2·OEt2
(25.8 mg, 0.1 mmol), dodecane (internal standard, 113.6 µL, 0.5 mmol), and chlorobenzene 1a (50.9
µL, 0.5 mmol) were added to an oven-dried Schleck tube containing a stirrer bar, followed by 1,4-
dioxane (3.0 mL), resulting in the formation of an orange suspension. In a separate dried Schlenk tube
the aryl boronate 2a (552.9 mg, 1.25 mmol) was dissolved in the 2-MeTHF (3.0 mL). Both Schlenk tubes
were sealed and taken out of the glove box and attached to a Schlenk line and heated to the
appropriate external temperature (2-MeTHF 80 °C and 1,4-dioxane 100 °C), whilst being stirred.
MeMgBr (0.05 mL, 1.0 M, 0.05 mmol) was added to the Schlenk tube containing the pre-catalyst
mixture and the resultant mixture was stirred for 5 mins. The aryl boronate-containing solution was
then added quickly to the Schlenk tube containing the pre-catalyst mixture, which was then sealed,
and the resultant reaction mixture was stirred and heated at 100 °C (external temp.). Aliquots (~0.05
mL) were taken at the times given. Each aliquot was quenched with 1.0 M HCl (0.1 mL) and extracted
into CH2Cl2 (2.0 mL) and then analysed by GC.

5.3 Determining the Orders in Pre-catalyst and Reagents | General Procedure 13: Kinetic experiments
The procedure below outlines the standard conditions that were employed in the kinetic experiments.
These were held constant when a given reaction component’s concentration was varied.
In an argon-filled glovebox, IMes·HCl (17.1 mg, 0.05 mmol), FeBr3 (14.8 mg, 0.05 mmol), MgBr2·OEt2
(25.8 mg, 0.1 mmol), dodecane (internal standard, 113.6 µL, 0.5 mmol), and chlorobenzene 1a (50.9
µL, 0.5 mmol) were added to an oven-dried Schleck tube containing a stirrer bar, followed by 1,4-
dioxane (3.0 mL), resulting in the formation of an orange suspension. In a separate dried Schlenk tube
the aryl boronate 2a (552.9 mg, 1.25 mmol) was dissolved in the 2-MeTHF (3.0 mL). Both Schlenk tubes
were sealed and taken out of the glove box and attached to a Schlenk line and heated to the
appropriate external temperature (2-MeTHF 80 °C and 1,4-dioxane 100 °C), whilst being stirred.
MeMgBr (0.05 mL, 1.0 M, 0.05 mmol) was added to the Schlenk tube containing the pre-catalyst
mixture and the resultant mixture was stirred for 5 mins. The aryl boronate-containing solution was
then added quickly to the Schlenk tube containing the pre-catalyst mixture, which was then sealed,
and the resultant reaction mixture was stirred and heated at 100 °C (external temp.). Aliquots (~0.05
mL) were taken at the times given. Each aliquot was quenched with 1.0 M HCl (0.1 mL) and extracted
into CH2Cl2 (2.0 mL) and then analysed by GC.

5.3 Determining the Orders in Pre-catalyst and Reagents | General Procedure 13: Kinetic experiments
The procedure below outlines the standard conditions that were employed in the kinetic experiments.
These were held constant when a given reaction component’s concentration was varied.
In an argon-filled glovebox, IMes·HCl (17.1 mg, 0.05 mmol), FeBr3 (14.8 mg, 0.05 mmol), MgBr2·OEt2
(25.8 mg, 0.1 mmol), dodecane (internal standard, 113.6 µL, 0.5 mmol), and chlorobenzene 1a (50.9
µL, 0.5 mmol) were added to an oven-dried Schleck tube containing a stirrer bar, followed by 1,4-
dioxane (3.0 mL), resulting in the formation of an orange suspension. In a separate dried Schlenk tube
the aryl boronate 2a (552.9 mg, 1.25 mmol) was dissolved in the 2-MeTHF (3.0 mL). Both Schlenk tubes
were sealed and taken out of the glove box and attached to a Schlenk line and heated to the
appropriate external temperature (2-MeTHF 80 °C and 1,4-dioxane 100 °C), whilst being stirred.
MeMgBr (0.05 mL, 1.0 M, 0.05 mmol) was added to the Schlenk tube containing the pre-catalyst
mixture and the resultant mixture was stirred for 5 mins. The aryl boronate-containing solution was
then added quickly to the Schlenk tube containing the pre-catalyst mixture, which was then sealed,
and the resultant reaction mixture was stirred and heated at 100 °C (external temp.). Aliquots (~0.05
mL) were taken at the times given. Each aliquot was quenched with 1.0 M HCl (0.1 mL) and extracted
into CH2Cl2 (2.0 mL) and then analysed by GC.
