5.3 Determining the Orders in Pre-catalyst and Reagents | General Procedure 13: Kinetic experiments
The procedure below outlines the standard conditions that were employed in the kinetic experiments.
These were held constant when a given reaction component’s concentration was varied.
In an argon-filled glovebox, IMes·HCl (17.1 mg, 0.05 mmol), FeBr3 (14.8 mg, 0.05 mmol), MgBr2·OEt2
(25.8 mg, 0.1 mmol), dodecane (internal standard, 113.6 µL, 0.5 mmol), and chlorobenzene 1a (50.9
µL, 0.5 mmol) were added to an oven-dried Schleck tube containing a stirrer bar, followed by 1,4-
dioxane (3.0 mL), resulting in the formation of an orange suspension. In a separate dried Schlenk tube
the aryl boronate 2a (552.9 mg, 1.25 mmol) was dissolved in the 2-MeTHF (3.0 mL). Both Schlenk tubes
were sealed and taken out of the glove box and attached to a Schlenk line and heated to the
appropriate external temperature (2-MeTHF 80 °C and 1,4-dioxane 100 °C), whilst being stirred.
MeMgBr (0.05 mL, 1.0 M, 0.05 mmol) was added to the Schlenk tube containing the pre-catalyst
mixture and the resultant mixture was stirred for 5 mins. The aryl boronate-containing solution was
then added quickly to the Schlenk tube containing the pre-catalyst mixture, which was then sealed,
and the resultant reaction mixture was stirred and heated at 100 °C (external temp.). Aliquots (~0.05
mL) were taken at the times given. Each aliquot was quenched with 1.0 M HCl (0.1 mL) and extracted
into CH2Cl2 (2.0 mL) and then analysed by GC.

5.3 Determining the Orders in Pre-catalyst and Reagents | General Procedure 13: Kinetic experiments
The procedure below outlines the standard conditions that were employed in the kinetic experiments.
These were held constant when a given reaction component’s concentration was varied.
In an argon-filled glovebox, IMes·HCl (17.1 mg, 0.05 mmol), FeBr3 (14.8 mg, 0.05 mmol), MgBr2·OEt2
(25.8 mg, 0.1 mmol), dodecane (internal standard, 113.6 µL, 0.5 mmol), and chlorobenzene 1a (50.9
µL, 0.5 mmol) were added to an oven-dried Schleck tube containing a stirrer bar, followed by 1,4-
dioxane (3.0 mL), resulting in the formation of an orange suspension. In a separate dried Schlenk tube
the aryl boronate 2a (552.9 mg, 1.25 mmol) was dissolved in the 2-MeTHF (3.0 mL). Both Schlenk tubes
were sealed and taken out of the glove box and attached to a Schlenk line and heated to the
appropriate external temperature (2-MeTHF 80 °C and 1,4-dioxane 100 °C), whilst being stirred.
MeMgBr (0.05 mL, 1.0 M, 0.05 mmol) was added to the Schlenk tube containing the pre-catalyst
mixture and the resultant mixture was stirred for 5 mins. The aryl boronate-containing solution was
then added quickly to the Schlenk tube containing the pre-catalyst mixture, which was then sealed,
and the resultant reaction mixture was stirred and heated at 100 °C (external temp.). Aliquots (~0.05
mL) were taken at the times given. Each aliquot was quenched with 1.0 M HCl (0.1 mL) and extracted
into CH2Cl2 (2.0 mL) and then analysed by GC.

5.3 Determining the Orders in Pre-catalyst and Reagents | General Procedure 13: Kinetic experiments
The procedure below outlines the standard conditions that were employed in the kinetic experiments.
These were held constant when a given reaction component’s concentration was varied.
In an argon-filled glovebox, IMes·HCl (17.1 mg, 0.05 mmol), FeBr3 (14.8 mg, 0.05 mmol), MgBr2·OEt2
(25.8 mg, 0.1 mmol), dodecane (internal standard, 113.6 µL, 0.5 mmol), and chlorobenzene 1a (50.9
µL, 0.5 mmol) were added to an oven-dried Schleck tube containing a stirrer bar, followed by 1,4-
dioxane (3.0 mL), resulting in the formation of an orange suspension. In a separate dried Schlenk tube
the aryl boronate 2a (552.9 mg, 1.25 mmol) was dissolved in the 2-MeTHF (3.0 mL). Both Schlenk tubes
were sealed and taken out of the glove box and attached to a Schlenk line and heated to the
appropriate external temperature (2-MeTHF 80 °C and 1,4-dioxane 100 °C), whilst being stirred.
MeMgBr (0.05 mL, 1.0 M, 0.05 mmol) was added to the Schlenk tube containing the pre-catalyst
mixture and the resultant mixture was stirred for 5 mins. The aryl boronate-containing solution was
then added quickly to the Schlenk tube containing the pre-catalyst mixture, which was then sealed,
and the resultant reaction mixture was stirred and heated at 100 °C (external temp.). Aliquots (~0.05
mL) were taken at the times given. Each aliquot was quenched with 1.0 M HCl (0.1 mL) and extracted
into CH2Cl2 (2.0 mL) and then analysed by GC.

5.3 Determining the Orders in Pre-catalyst and Reagents | General Procedure 13: Kinetic experiments
The procedure below outlines the standard conditions that were employed in the kinetic experiments.
These were held constant when a given reaction component’s concentration was varied.
In an argon-filled glovebox, IMes·HCl (17.1 mg, 0.05 mmol), FeBr3 (14.8 mg, 0.05 mmol), MgBr2·OEt2
(25.8 mg, 0.1 mmol), dodecane (internal standard, 113.6 µL, 0.5 mmol), and chlorobenzene 1a (50.9
µL, 0.5 mmol) were added to an oven-dried Schleck tube containing a stirrer bar, followed by 1,4-
dioxane (3.0 mL), resulting in the formation of an orange suspension. In a separate dried Schlenk tube
the aryl boronate 2a (552.9 mg, 1.25 mmol) was dissolved in the 2-MeTHF (3.0 mL). Both Schlenk tubes
were sealed and taken out of the glove box and attached to a Schlenk line and heated to the
appropriate external temperature (2-MeTHF 80 °C and 1,4-dioxane 100 °C), whilst being stirred.
MeMgBr (0.05 mL, 1.0 M, 0.05 mmol) was added to the Schlenk tube containing the pre-catalyst
mixture and the resultant mixture was stirred for 5 mins. The aryl boronate-containing solution was
then added quickly to the Schlenk tube containing the pre-catalyst mixture, which was then sealed,
and the resultant reaction mixture was stirred and heated at 100 °C (external temp.). Aliquots (~0.05
mL) were taken at the times given. Each aliquot was quenched with 1.0 M HCl (0.1 mL) and extracted
into CH2Cl2 (2.0 mL) and then analysed by GC.

5.3 Determining the Orders in Pre-catalyst and Reagents | General Procedure 13: Kinetic experiments
The procedure below outlines the standard conditions that were employed in the kinetic experiments.
These were held constant when a given reaction component’s concentration was varied.
In an argon-filled glovebox, IMes·HCl (17.1 mg, 0.05 mmol), FeBr3 (14.8 mg, 0.05 mmol), MgBr2·OEt2
(25.8 mg, 0.1 mmol), dodecane (internal standard, 113.6 µL, 0.5 mmol), and chlorobenzene 1a (50.9
µL, 0.5 mmol) were added to an oven-dried Schleck tube containing a stirrer bar, followed by 1,4-
dioxane (3.0 mL), resulting in the formation of an orange suspension. In a separate dried Schlenk tube
the aryl boronate 2a (552.9 mg, 1.25 mmol) was dissolved in the 2-MeTHF (3.0 mL). Both Schlenk tubes
were sealed and taken out of the glove box and attached to a Schlenk line and heated to the
appropriate external temperature (2-MeTHF 80 °C and 1,4-dioxane 100 °C), whilst being stirred.
MeMgBr (0.05 mL, 1.0 M, 0.05 mmol) was added to the Schlenk tube containing the pre-catalyst
mixture and the resultant mixture was stirred for 5 mins. The aryl boronate-containing solution was
then added quickly to the Schlenk tube containing the pre-catalyst mixture, which was then sealed,
and the resultant reaction mixture was stirred and heated at 100 °C (external temp.). Aliquots (~0.05
mL) were taken at the times given. Each aliquot was quenched with 1.0 M HCl (0.1 mL) and extracted
into CH2Cl2 (2.0 mL) and then analysed by GC.

5.3 Determining the Orders in Pre-catalyst and Reagents | General Procedure 13: Kinetic experiments
The procedure below outlines the standard conditions that were employed in the kinetic experiments.
These were held constant when a given reaction component’s concentration was varied.
In an argon-filled glovebox, IMes·HCl (17.1 mg, 0.05 mmol), FeBr3 (14.8 mg, 0.05 mmol), MgBr2·OEt2
(25.8 mg, 0.1 mmol), dodecane (internal standard, 113.6 µL, 0.5 mmol), and chlorobenzene 1a (50.9
µL, 0.5 mmol) were added to an oven-dried Schleck tube containing a stirrer bar, followed by 1,4-
dioxane (3.0 mL), resulting in the formation of an orange suspension. In a separate dried Schlenk tube
the aryl boronate 2a (552.9 mg, 1.25 mmol) was dissolved in the 2-MeTHF (3.0 mL). Both Schlenk tubes
were sealed and taken out of the glove box and attached to a Schlenk line and heated to the
appropriate external temperature (2-MeTHF 80 °C and 1,4-dioxane 100 °C), whilst being stirred.
MeMgBr (0.05 mL, 1.0 M, 0.05 mmol) was added to the Schlenk tube containing the pre-catalyst
mixture and the resultant mixture was stirred for 5 mins. The aryl boronate-containing solution was
then added quickly to the Schlenk tube containing the pre-catalyst mixture, which was then sealed,
and the resultant reaction mixture was stirred and heated at 100 °C (external temp.). Aliquots (~0.05
mL) were taken at the times given. Each aliquot was quenched with 1.0 M HCl (0.1 mL) and extracted
into CH2Cl2 (2.0 mL) and then analysed by GC.

5.3 Determining the Orders in Pre-catalyst and Reagents | General Procedure 13: Kinetic experiments
The procedure below outlines the standard conditions that were employed in the kinetic experiments.
These were held constant when a given reaction component’s concentration was varied.
In an argon-filled glovebox, IMes·HCl (17.1 mg, 0.05 mmol), FeBr3 (14.8 mg, 0.05 mmol), MgBr2·OEt2
(25.8 mg, 0.1 mmol), dodecane (internal standard, 113.6 µL, 0.5 mmol), and chlorobenzene 1a (50.9
µL, 0.5 mmol) were added to an oven-dried Schleck tube containing a stirrer bar, followed by 1,4-
dioxane (3.0 mL), resulting in the formation of an orange suspension. In a separate dried Schlenk tube
the aryl boronate 2a (552.9 mg, 1.25 mmol) was dissolved in the 2-MeTHF (3.0 mL). Both Schlenk tubes
were sealed and taken out of the glove box and attached to a Schlenk line and heated to the
appropriate external temperature (2-MeTHF 80 °C and 1,4-dioxane 100 °C), whilst being stirred.
MeMgBr (0.05 mL, 1.0 M, 0.05 mmol) was added to the Schlenk tube containing the pre-catalyst
mixture and the resultant mixture was stirred for 5 mins. The aryl boronate-containing solution was
then added quickly to the Schlenk tube containing the pre-catalyst mixture, which was then sealed,
and the resultant reaction mixture was stirred and heated at 100 °C (external temp.). Aliquots (~0.05
mL) were taken at the times given. Each aliquot was quenched with 1.0 M HCl (0.1 mL) and extracted
into CH2Cl2 (2.0 mL) and then analysed by GC.

5.3 Determining the Orders in Pre-catalyst and Reagents | General Procedure 13: Kinetic experiments
The procedure below outlines the standard conditions that were employed in the kinetic experiments.
These were held constant when a given reaction component’s concentration was varied.
In an argon-filled glovebox, IMes·HCl (17.1 mg, 0.05 mmol), FeBr3 (14.8 mg, 0.05 mmol), MgBr2·OEt2
(25.8 mg, 0.1 mmol), dodecane (internal standard, 113.6 µL, 0.5 mmol), and chlorobenzene 1a (50.9
µL, 0.5 mmol) were added to an oven-dried Schleck tube containing a stirrer bar, followed by 1,4-
dioxane (3.0 mL), resulting in the formation of an orange suspension. In a separate dried Schlenk tube
the aryl boronate 2a (552.9 mg, 1.25 mmol) was dissolved in the 2-MeTHF (3.0 mL). Both Schlenk tubes
were sealed and taken out of the glove box and attached to a Schlenk line and heated to the
appropriate external temperature (2-MeTHF 80 °C and 1,4-dioxane 100 °C), whilst being stirred.
MeMgBr (0.05 mL, 1.0 M, 0.05 mmol) was added to the Schlenk tube containing the pre-catalyst
mixture and the resultant mixture was stirred for 5 mins. The aryl boronate-containing solution was
then added quickly to the Schlenk tube containing the pre-catalyst mixture, which was then sealed,
and the resultant reaction mixture was stirred and heated at 100 °C (external temp.). Aliquots (~0.05
mL) were taken at the times given. Each aliquot was quenched with 1.0 M HCl (0.1 mL) and extracted
into CH2Cl2 (2.0 mL) and then analysed by GC.

5.3 Determining the Orders in Pre-catalyst and Reagents | General Procedure 13: Kinetic experiments
The procedure below outlines the standard conditions that were employed in the kinetic experiments.
These were held constant when a given reaction component’s concentration was varied.
In an argon-filled glovebox, IMes·HCl (17.1 mg, 0.05 mmol), FeBr3 (14.8 mg, 0.05 mmol), MgBr2·OEt2
(25.8 mg, 0.1 mmol), dodecane (internal standard, 113.6 µL, 0.5 mmol), and chlorobenzene 1a (50.9
µL, 0.5 mmol) were added to an oven-dried Schleck tube containing a stirrer bar, followed by 1,4-
dioxane (3.0 mL), resulting in the formation of an orange suspension. In a separate dried Schlenk tube
the aryl boronate 2a (552.9 mg, 1.25 mmol) was dissolved in the 2-MeTHF (3.0 mL). Both Schlenk tubes
were sealed and taken out of the glove box and attached to a Schlenk line and heated to the
appropriate external temperature (2-MeTHF 80 °C and 1,4-dioxane 100 °C), whilst being stirred.
MeMgBr (0.05 mL, 1.0 M, 0.05 mmol) was added to the Schlenk tube containing the pre-catalyst
mixture and the resultant mixture was stirred for 5 mins. The aryl boronate-containing solution was
then added quickly to the Schlenk tube containing the pre-catalyst mixture, which was then sealed,
and the resultant reaction mixture was stirred and heated at 100 °C (external temp.). Aliquots (~0.05
mL) were taken at the times given. Each aliquot was quenched with 1.0 M HCl (0.1 mL) and extracted
into CH2Cl2 (2.0 mL) and then analysed by GC.

5.3 Determining the Orders in Pre-catalyst and Reagents | General Procedure 13: Kinetic experiments
The procedure below outlines the standard conditions that were employed in the kinetic experiments.
These were held constant when a given reaction component’s concentration was varied.
In an argon-filled glovebox, IMes·HCl (17.1 mg, 0.05 mmol), FeBr3 (14.8 mg, 0.05 mmol), MgBr2·OEt2
(25.8 mg, 0.1 mmol), dodecane (internal standard, 113.6 µL, 0.5 mmol), and chlorobenzene 1a (50.9
µL, 0.5 mmol) were added to an oven-dried Schleck tube containing a stirrer bar, followed by 1,4-
dioxane (3.0 mL), resulting in the formation of an orange suspension. In a separate dried Schlenk tube
the aryl boronate 2a (552.9 mg, 1.25 mmol) was dissolved in the 2-MeTHF (3.0 mL). Both Schlenk tubes
were sealed and taken out of the glove box and attached to a Schlenk line and heated to the
appropriate external temperature (2-MeTHF 80 °C and 1,4-dioxane 100 °C), whilst being stirred.
MeMgBr (0.05 mL, 1.0 M, 0.05 mmol) was added to the Schlenk tube containing the pre-catalyst
mixture and the resultant mixture was stirred for 5 mins. The aryl boronate-containing solution was
then added quickly to the Schlenk tube containing the pre-catalyst mixture, which was then sealed,
and the resultant reaction mixture was stirred and heated at 100 °C (external temp.). Aliquots (~0.05
mL) were taken at the times given. Each aliquot was quenched with 1.0 M HCl (0.1 mL) and extracted
into CH2Cl2 (2.0 mL) and then analysed by GC.

5.3 Determining the Orders in Pre-catalyst and Reagents | General Procedure 13: Kinetic experiments
The procedure below outlines the standard conditions that were employed in the kinetic experiments.
These were held constant when a given reaction component’s concentration was varied.
In an argon-filled glovebox, IMes·HCl (17.1 mg, 0.05 mmol), FeBr3 (14.8 mg, 0.05 mmol), MgBr2·OEt2
(25.8 mg, 0.1 mmol), dodecane (internal standard, 113.6 µL, 0.5 mmol), and chlorobenzene 1a (50.9
µL, 0.5 mmol) were added to an oven-dried Schleck tube containing a stirrer bar, followed by 1,4-
dioxane (3.0 mL), resulting in the formation of an orange suspension. In a separate dried Schlenk tube
the aryl boronate 2a (552.9 mg, 1.25 mmol) was dissolved in the 2-MeTHF (3.0 mL). Both Schlenk tubes
were sealed and taken out of the glove box and attached to a Schlenk line and heated to the
appropriate external temperature (2-MeTHF 80 °C and 1,4-dioxane 100 °C), whilst being stirred.
MeMgBr (0.05 mL, 1.0 M, 0.05 mmol) was added to the Schlenk tube containing the pre-catalyst
mixture and the resultant mixture was stirred for 5 mins. The aryl boronate-containing solution was
then added quickly to the Schlenk tube containing the pre-catalyst mixture, which was then sealed,
and the resultant reaction mixture was stirred and heated at 100 °C (external temp.). Aliquots (~0.05
mL) were taken at the times given. Each aliquot was quenched with 1.0 M HCl (0.1 mL) and extracted
into CH2Cl2 (2.0 mL) and then analysed by GC.

5.3 Determining the Orders in Pre-catalyst and Reagents | General Procedure 13: Kinetic experiments
The procedure below outlines the standard conditions that were employed in the kinetic experiments.
These were held constant when a given reaction component’s concentration was varied.
In an argon-filled glovebox, IMes·HCl (17.1 mg, 0.05 mmol), FeBr3 (14.8 mg, 0.05 mmol), MgBr2·OEt2
(25.8 mg, 0.1 mmol), dodecane (internal standard, 113.6 µL, 0.5 mmol), and chlorobenzene 1a (50.9
µL, 0.5 mmol) were added to an oven-dried Schleck tube containing a stirrer bar, followed by 1,4-
dioxane (3.0 mL), resulting in the formation of an orange suspension. In a separate dried Schlenk tube
the aryl boronate 2a (552.9 mg, 1.25 mmol) was dissolved in the 2-MeTHF (3.0 mL). Both Schlenk tubes
were sealed and taken out of the glove box and attached to a Schlenk line and heated to the
appropriate external temperature (2-MeTHF 80 °C and 1,4-dioxane 100 °C), whilst being stirred.
MeMgBr (0.05 mL, 1.0 M, 0.05 mmol) was added to the Schlenk tube containing the pre-catalyst
mixture and the resultant mixture was stirred for 5 mins. The aryl boronate-containing solution was
then added quickly to the Schlenk tube containing the pre-catalyst mixture, which was then sealed,
and the resultant reaction mixture was stirred and heated at 100 °C (external temp.). Aliquots (~0.05
mL) were taken at the times given. Each aliquot was quenched with 1.0 M HCl (0.1 mL) and extracted
into CH2Cl2 (2.0 mL) and then analysed by GC.

5.3 Determining the Orders in Pre-catalyst and Reagents | General Procedure 13: Kinetic experiments
The procedure below outlines the standard conditions that were employed in the kinetic experiments.
These were held constant when a given reaction component’s concentration was varied.
In an argon-filled glovebox, IMes·HCl (17.1 mg, 0.05 mmol), FeBr3 (14.8 mg, 0.05 mmol), MgBr2·OEt2
(25.8 mg, 0.1 mmol), dodecane (internal standard, 113.6 µL, 0.5 mmol), and chlorobenzene 1a (50.9
µL, 0.5 mmol) were added to an oven-dried Schleck tube containing a stirrer bar, followed by 1,4-
dioxane (3.0 mL), resulting in the formation of an orange suspension. In a separate dried Schlenk tube
the aryl boronate 2a (552.9 mg, 1.25 mmol) was dissolved in the 2-MeTHF (3.0 mL). Both Schlenk tubes
were sealed and taken out of the glove box and attached to a Schlenk line and heated to the
appropriate external temperature (2-MeTHF 80 °C and 1,4-dioxane 100 °C), whilst being stirred.
MeMgBr (0.05 mL, 1.0 M, 0.05 mmol) was added to the Schlenk tube containing the pre-catalyst
mixture and the resultant mixture was stirred for 5 mins. The aryl boronate-containing solution was
then added quickly to the Schlenk tube containing the pre-catalyst mixture, which was then sealed,
and the resultant reaction mixture was stirred and heated at 100 °C (external temp.). Aliquots (~0.05
mL) were taken at the times given. Each aliquot was quenched with 1.0 M HCl (0.1 mL) and extracted
into CH2Cl2 (2.0 mL) and then analysed by GC.

5.3 Determining the Orders in Pre-catalyst and Reagents | General Procedure 13: Kinetic experiments
The procedure below outlines the standard conditions that were employed in the kinetic experiments.
These were held constant when a given reaction component’s concentration was varied.
In an argon-filled glovebox, IMes·HCl (17.1 mg, 0.05 mmol), FeBr3 (14.8 mg, 0.05 mmol), MgBr2·OEt2
(25.8 mg, 0.1 mmol), dodecane (internal standard, 113.6 µL, 0.5 mmol), and chlorobenzene 1a (50.9
µL, 0.5 mmol) were added to an oven-dried Schleck tube containing a stirrer bar, followed by 1,4-
dioxane (3.0 mL), resulting in the formation of an orange suspension. In a separate dried Schlenk tube
the aryl boronate 2a (552.9 mg, 1.25 mmol) was dissolved in the 2-MeTHF (3.0 mL). Both Schlenk tubes
were sealed and taken out of the glove box and attached to a Schlenk line and heated to the
appropriate external temperature (2-MeTHF 80 °C and 1,4-dioxane 100 °C), whilst being stirred.
MeMgBr (0.05 mL, 1.0 M, 0.05 mmol) was added to the Schlenk tube containing the pre-catalyst
mixture and the resultant mixture was stirred for 5 mins. The aryl boronate-containing solution was
then added quickly to the Schlenk tube containing the pre-catalyst mixture, which was then sealed,
and the resultant reaction mixture was stirred and heated at 100 °C (external temp.). Aliquots (~0.05
mL) were taken at the times given. Each aliquot was quenched with 1.0 M HCl (0.1 mL) and extracted
into CH2Cl2 (2.0 mL) and then analysed by GC.

5.3 Determining the Orders in Pre-catalyst and Reagents | General Procedure 13: Kinetic experiments
The procedure below outlines the standard conditions that were employed in the kinetic experiments.
These were held constant when a given reaction component’s concentration was varied.
In an argon-filled glovebox, IMes·HCl (17.1 mg, 0.05 mmol), FeBr3 (14.8 mg, 0.05 mmol), MgBr2·OEt2
(25.8 mg, 0.1 mmol), dodecane (internal standard, 113.6 µL, 0.5 mmol), and chlorobenzene 1a (50.9
µL, 0.5 mmol) were added to an oven-dried Schleck tube containing a stirrer bar, followed by 1,4-
dioxane (3.0 mL), resulting in the formation of an orange suspension. In a separate dried Schlenk tube
the aryl boronate 2a (552.9 mg, 1.25 mmol) was dissolved in the 2-MeTHF (3.0 mL). Both Schlenk tubes
were sealed and taken out of the glove box and attached to a Schlenk line and heated to the
appropriate external temperature (2-MeTHF 80 °C and 1,4-dioxane 100 °C), whilst being stirred.
MeMgBr (0.05 mL, 1.0 M, 0.05 mmol) was added to the Schlenk tube containing the pre-catalyst
mixture and the resultant mixture was stirred for 5 mins. The aryl boronate-containing solution was
then added quickly to the Schlenk tube containing the pre-catalyst mixture, which was then sealed,
and the resultant reaction mixture was stirred and heated at 100 °C (external temp.). Aliquots (~0.05
mL) were taken at the times given. Each aliquot was quenched with 1.0 M HCl (0.1 mL) and extracted
into CH2Cl2 (2.0 mL) and then analysed by GC.

In an argon-filled glovebox, IMes·HCl (17.1 mg, 0.05 mmol), FeBr3 (14.8 mg, 0.05 mmol), MgBr2·OEt2
(25.8 mg, 0.1 mmol), dodecane (internal standard, 113.6 µL, 0.5 mmol), and aryl chloride 1 (0.5 mmol)
were added to a dried Schleck tube, containing a stirrer bar, followed by 1,4-dioxane (3.0 mL), forming
a suspension. In a separate dried Schlenk tube the aryl boronate 2b (552.9 mg, 1.25 mmol) was
dissolved in the 2-MeTHF (3.0 mL). Both Schlenk tubes were sealed and taken out of the glove box and
attached to a Schlenk line and heated to the appropriate external temperature (2-MeTHF 80 °C and
1,4-dioxane 100 °C), whilst being stirred. MeMgBr (0.05 mL, 1.0 M, 0.05 mmol) was added to the
Schlenk tube containing the pre-catalyst mixture and the resultant mixture was stirred for 5 mins. The
aryl boronate-containing solution was then added quickly to the Schlenk tube containing the pre-
catalyst mixture, which was then sealed, and the resultant reaction mixture was stirred and heated at
100 °C (external temp.). Aliquots (~0.05 mL) were taken at the times given. Each aliquot was quenched
with 1.0 M HCl (0.1 mL) and extracted into CH2Cl2 (2.0 mL) and then analysed by GC.
General Procedure 15: Data collection for linear free energy relationship on changing para-
substituents nucleophile
Under an N2 atmosphere, an oven dried Schlenk tube was charged with the appropriate boronic ester
(1.25 mmol) and was dissolved in 2-MeTHF (3.0 mL) and cooled to -40 °C. tBuLi (1.7 M in hexane, 0.74
mL, 1.25 mmol) was then added dropwise and allowed to stir for 30 mins at -40 °C. The reaction
mixture was slowly brought to rt and stirred for a further 45 mins.
86 Meanwhile, in an argon-filled glovebox, IMes·HCl (17.1 mg, 0.05 mmol), FeBr3 (14.8 mg, 0.05 mmol), MgBr2·OEt2 (25.8 mg, 0.1 mmol), dodecane (internal standard, 113.6 µL, 0.5 mmol), and chlorobenzene 1a (50.9 µL, 0.5 mmol) were added to a dried Schleck tube, containing a stirrer bar, followed by 1,4-dioxane (3.0 mL), forming an orange suspension. The Schlenk tube was sealed and taken out of the glovebox and attached to a Schlenk line and heated to an external temperature of 100 °C. MeMgBr (0.05 mL, 1.0 M, 0.05 mmol) was added to the Schlenk tube containing the precatalyst mixture and the resultant mixture was stirred for 5 mins. The aryl boronate 2 formed in situ, was then added in one portion to the Schlenk containing the pre-catalyst mixture, sealed, and reacted at 100 °C and aliquots (~0.05 mL) were taken at the times given. Each aliquot was quenched with 1.0 M HCl (0.1 mL) and extracted into CH2Cl2 (2.0 mL) and then analysed by GC.

with 1.0 M HCl (0.1 mL) and extracted into CH2Cl2 (2.0 mL) and then analysed by GC.

5.6 Mass Balance Study | In an argon-filled glovebox, IMes·HCl (17.1 mg, 0.05 mmol), FeBr3 (14.8 mg, 0.05 mmol), MgBr2·OEt2
(25.8 mg, 0.1 mmol) and 1-chloro-4-fluorobenzene (53 μL, 0.5 mmol) were added to a dried Schlenk
tube containing a stirrer bar, followed by 1,4-dioxane (3.0 mL), resulting in an orange suspension. In a
separate dried Schlenk tube the aryl boronate 2a (552.9 mg, 1.25 mmol) was dissolved in the 2-MeTHF
(3.0 mL). Both Schlenk tubes were sealed and taken out of the glove box and attached to a Schlenk
line and heated to the appropriate external temperature (2-MeTHF 80 °C and 1,4-dioxane 100 °C),
whilst being stirred. MeMgBr (0.05 mL, 1.0 M, 0.05 mmol) was added to the Schlenk tube containing
the pre-catalyst mixture and the resultant mixture was stirred for 5 mins. The aryl boronate-containing
solution was then added quickly to the Schlenk tube containing the pre-catalyst mixture and the
resultant mixture heated at 100 °C (external temp.) for 3 hrs. The resulting mixture was cooled to
room temperature and quenched with 1.0 M HCl (5.0 mL). The organics were extracted with CH2Cl2 (3
x 10 mL), the combined organics layers dried over MgSO4 and filtered. 1,3,5-Trimethoxybenzene
(internal standard, 84.1 mg, 0.5 mmol) and α,α,α-trifluorotoluene (internal standard, 61.4 μL,
0.5mmol) were added, and an aliquot taken for analysis by 1H- and 19F-NMR spectroscopy. The
volatiles were then removed under vacuum.

5.7 Radical Trap Investigation | Radical probe experiments were undertaken using 1,4-cyclohexadiene, butylated hydroxytoluene
(BHT), 1,1-diphenylethylene, 2,2,6,6-tetramethylpiperidine-1-oxyl (TEMPO), and trityl chloride. In an
argon-filled glovebox, IMes·HCl (17.2 mg, 0.05 mmol) and FeBr3 (14.8 mg, 0.05 mmol) were added to
a dried Schleck tube, containing a stirrer bar, followed by 1,4-dioxane (3.0 mL), and the resultant
mixture was stirred for 30 min at rt during which time an orange suspension formed. MgBr2·OEt2 (25.8
mg, 0.1 mmol) and chlorobenzene 1a (51 µL, 0.5 mmol) were then added. In a separate Schlenk tube
the aryl boronate 2a (552.9 mg, 1.25 mmol) was dissolved in 2-MeTHF (3.0 mL). Both Schlenk tubes
were sealed and taken out of the glove box and attached to a Schlenk line and heated to the
appropriate temperature (2-MeTHF 80 °C and 1,4-dioxane 100 °C), whilst being stirred. In all cases
MeMgBr was used, this was added as a solution (0.05 mL, 1.0 M in Et2O, 0.05 mmol) to the Schlenk
tube containing the pre-catalyst mixture and the resultant mixture was stirred for 5 mins, this was
followed by the appropriate additive (0.5 mmol) and the mixture allowed to stir for 5 mins. The aryl
boronate-containing solution was then added quickly to the Schlenk tube containing the pre-catalyst
mixture, which was then sealed, and the resultant reaction mixture was stirred and heated at 100 °C
for 18 h. The resulting mixture was cooled to room temperature and quenched with 1.0 M HCl (2.5
mL) and dodecane (internal standard, 113.6 µL, 0.5 mmol) was added. The organics were extracted
into CH2Cl2 (10 mL), and an aliquot was taken for analysis by GC and GCMS.
